75	> **Auth-boundary discipline (per [ADR 0010](adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md)):** new connection-CRUD endpoints (and every protected route from here on) depend on a generic internal "current user" dependency that returns DataQ's own `User` — they must NOT read MSAL token claims directly in route/service code. Cheap now; expensive to retrofit once dozens of endpoints exist. No new abstraction layer required, just the boundary.

Rotation persists before the probe, so a bad new credential surfaces as 502 `connection_test_failed`; a store-write failure is 502 `connection_secret_write_failed` with the old credential untouched. 6 TestClient tests (rotate+verify ok, failed-verify-but-rotation-persists, write-fail 502, 404, secret-required 422). Type-agnostic — applies to all six connection types

133	### Column profiler (3 tasks — 3/3 ✅)
134	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Snowflake) — nulls, distinct count, min / max, top values — `profile_service` + `POST /suites/{id}/profile` (require_permission **edit**, suite-scoped so the connection is access-gated). Reads-only, persists nothing: one aggregate query (row count + null/distinct/min/max per column) + one top-N-values query per column, then `assemble_profile`. **SQL-injection-safe** — queries are built with the **SQLAlchemy Core expression language** (`select`/`table`/`column`, dialect-quoted) so there's no raw-string SQL sink (no S608/B608/CodeQL `py/sql-injection`); identifiers are additionally allowlist-validated (`validate_identifier`, strict `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$`) as defence-in-depth + a clean early 422, and `top_n` is `int()`-coerced. v1 → 422: non-Snowflake type (dispatch generalises Week 5), bad identifier, no schema; execution failure → 502 (adapter exception never echoed). min/max/top-values NaN-sanitised. 28 tests (22 pure: identifier allowlist incl. injection strings, compiled-SQL builders, assembly, div-by-zero, NaN; 6 endpoint via fake conn: stats, injection-422, unsupported-type-422, 502, edit-gated, no-schema-422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 90% (live `_open_connection` is the deferred warehouse seam)
135	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (ADLS / S3) — same stats via Pandas on sampled file — extended `profile_service` into a type dispatcher (`profile_connection`): SQL types → in-warehouse aggregation (unchanged), flat-file types (`adls_gen2`/`s3`) → download a **sample** of the file into Pandas and compute the same stats (`profile_dataframe`). Same `POST /suites/{id}/profile` endpoint, now polymorphic: SQL targets pass `table`/`schema`, flat-file targets pass `path` (+ optional `file_format`, else inferred from extension); response carries whichever identity applies. CSV + Parquet. **pandas "load less data" levers** (per the user's scale.html prompt): column projection (CSV `usecols`, Parquet `columns=` via pyarrow schema) so profiling 3 of N columns doesn't read all N, + row sampling (`_SAMPLE_ROWS`), + **zero-copy Arrow-backed dtypes** on the Parquet read (`dtype_backend="pyarrow"` — parquet is already Arrow, kept zero-copy; the stat helpers + `_to_native` are Arrow-scalar/`pd.NA`-safe). Stats are vectorised pandas (no Python row loops — enhancingperf N/A; CoW is a no-op for a read-only profiler + a process-global flag, so not toggled; pyarrow CSV engine rejected — it's incompatible with `nrows`/callable-`usecols`). NaN/Timestamp→JSON-safe. v1 → 422: unsupported type (UC still pending), missing target, unknown format, missing column; read failure → 502 (exception never echoed). Reuses `ColumnProfile`/`ProfileResult`. 24 new tests (pure `profile_dataframe`/`infer_file_format`/`_to_native`/projection-parse + endpoint via fake `_read_dataframe`); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 85% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). _Deferred: streaming/range reads (whole object still downloaded before sampling) + out-of-core (Dask) — future work if profiling cost bites._
136	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Unity Catalog) — via Databricks SQL Warehouse — added `unity_catalog` to the profiler's **SQL** branch (reuses `profile_table` + the SQLAlchemy Core query builders + `assemble_profile` — no duplicate aggregation logic). `_open_connection` now dispatches the engine by type (`_engine_args`): Snowflake URL or a `REDACTED` URL via the installed `databricks` SQLAlchemy dialect. UC's **3-level namespace** (`catalog.schema.table`) is handled by building the table with a `quoted_name(f"{catalog}.{schema}", quote=False)` so the dialect emits three dotted parts rather than quoting the dotted string as one — verified by compiling the real builders against the Databricks dialect. Injection-safe: every part (catalog/schema/table/column) is allowlist-validated (no raw-string SQL, no CodeQL py/sql-injection surface). Endpoint gained `catalog` (request + response); the dispatcher requires it for UC (`422 profile_target_invalid` if absent). 12 new tests (catalog-aware builders compiled to SQL, `_engine_args` URL dispatch, UC endpoint stats via the same fake conn, missing-catalog 422, bad-catalog-identifier 422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 86% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). **Completes the column profiler across all 4 datasources.**

138	### Flat file check specifics (2 tasks — 2/2 ✅)
139	- [x] ✅ Check types for flat files: schema validation, row count, null checks, ~~freshness by filename date~~ — `FlatFileCheckRunner` (`datasources/flatfile.py`): downloads the file (S3/ADLS) into a pandas DataFrame and runs the suite's GX expectations against GX's **pandas DataFrame asset**, so all GX expectation-kind checks (schema/row-count/null/value checks) run against flat files. Extracted the shared GX machinery — snake_case→GX-class translation, GX-result→`SuiteOutcome` mapping, and the suite/validation-definition `run_expectations` flow — into `datasources/gx_runner.py` (reused by the Snowflake runner and the future UC runner; no duplication). Flat-file IO (`download_bytes` + full-file `read_dataframe`) moved to `flatfile.py` behind primitives (raw config + resolved secret, not the ORM — matches `build_snowflake_runner`), and the column profiler now shares it. Because GX runs **in-process on the DataFrame**, the run path is fully unit-tested with a canned frame (real GX execution, not mocked) — only the network download is the deferred-smoke seam. 16 new tests; `gx_runner` 100%, `flatfile` 76% (only `download_bytes` uncovered). _Connection-type → runner dispatch (Snowflake vs flat-file) is the Week-5 `run_suite` wiring; **freshness-by-filename** is the reserved `freshness` monitor kind (deferred, ADR 0012), not a GX expectation._
140	- [x] ✅ Batch resolution — resolve batching regex to matched files, pick latest or specific batch — `resolve_batch` (`datasources/flatfile.py`): a batch `pattern` is a regex whose **first capture group is the batch key**; `latest` selects the greatest key (lexicographic — ISO dates sort chronologically), falling back to the storage modified-time when the pattern has no group; `specific` selects the file whose key equals a given `batch`. `BatchNotFoundError` on no match / unknown batch. The filter+select logic is pure and fully unit-tested (8 tests); object listing (`list_files` — S3 `list_objects_v2` paginated / ADLS `list_blobs`) is the live seam, and `resolve_batch_file` composes list+resolve. _Wiring a check's target to a resolved batch path is the Week-5 `run_suite` dispatch._

143	- [x] ✅ UC table check path — UC table → GX DataFrame datasource → run suite — `UnityCatalogCheckRunner` (`datasources/unity_catalog.py`): reads the target table from the Databricks SQL Warehouse into a pandas DataFrame (`pd.read_sql_table` via the databricks SQLAlchemy dialect — reflection quotes identifiers, so no hand-built SQL) and runs the suite's GX expectations against GX's **pandas DataFrame asset** — the "GX DataFrame datasource" shape (§5), the same shape Databricks Labs DQX consumes, so v1.1 swaps GX→DQX behind this one interface. Reuses the shared `gx_runner` (`run_expectations` + result mapping) exactly like the flat-file runner; the `catalog` is pinned in the connection URL (`build_databricks_url`, now shared with the column profiler — no duplication) so the 2-level `schema.table` resolves to `catalog.schema.table`. Because GX runs **in-process on the DataFrame**, the run path is unit-tested with a canned frame (real GX execution); only the reflect+read (`_read_table`) is the deferred-smoke seam. `build_unity_catalog_runner` mirrors `build_snowflake_runner` (raw config + resolved PAT, not the ORM). 14 tests; `unity_catalog` 91% (only `_read_table` uncovered). _Connection-type → runner dispatch is the Week-5 `run_suite` wiring._

1	import { Alert, Button, Descriptions, type FormInstance, Flex, Tag, Typography } from 'antd';
2	import { useState } from 'react';
3	
4	import type { ResultStatus } from '../../api/runs';
5	import { type CheckDryRunResult, dryRunCheck } from '../../api/suites';
6	import { RESULT_STATUS_COLORS } from '../results/resultsFormat';
7	import { buildCheckPayload } from './checkForm';
8	
9	/**
10	 * Inline "preview before saving" affordance for the check editor: runs the
11	 * in-progress check against the suite's live target via the dry-run API
12	 * (`POST /suites/{id}/checks/dryrun`) and shows the severity outcome — without
13	 * persisting a Run/Result. Shared by the create page (`CheckNew`) and the edit
14	 * drawer (`CheckDrawer`); both pass the suite's run target (#215) so the same
15	 * `table`/`schema` the run would use is previewed.
16	 *
17	 * v1 backend limits (surfaced as the API's error message): dry-run needs a
18	 * table target and a Snowflake connection. The button is disabled (with a
19	 * reason) until an expectation is picked and the suite has a table target;
20	 * everything else (no credential, unreachable warehouse, wrong datasource) comes
21	 * back as a clean error from the API and renders in the alert.
22	 */
23	export function DryRunPreview({
24	  suiteId,
25	  expectationType,
26	  target,
27	  form,
28	}: {
29	  suiteId: string;
30	  expectationType: string | undefined;
31	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
32	  form: FormInstance;
33	}) {
34	  const [state, setState] = useState<
35	    | { status: 'idle' }
36	    | { status: 'running' }
37	    | { status: 'ok'; result: CheckDryRunResult }
38	    | { status: 'error'; error: string }
39	  >({ status: 'idle' });
40	
41	  // Clear a previous preview when the expectation changes — in the edit drawer
42	  // the picker switches type in-place (DryRunPreview stays mounted), so without
43	  // this the old result would linger, misattributed to the new expectation.
44	  // Render-phase reset (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern)
45	  // rather than an effect, so the stale result never paints.
46	  const [prevExpectation, setPrevExpectation] = useState(expectationType);
47	  if (expectationType !== prevExpectation) {
48	    setPrevExpectation(expectationType);
49	    setState({ status: 'idle' });
50	  }
51	
52	  const table = typeof target?.table === 'string' ? target.table : undefined;
53	  const schema = typeof target?.schema === 'string' ? target.schema : null;
54	
55	  const disabledReason = !expectationType
56	    ? 'Pick an expectation to preview it.'
57	    : !table
58	      ? 'Set a table target on the suite to preview against live data.'
59	      : undefined;
60	
61	  const run = async () => {
62	    if (!expectationType || !table) return;
63	    setState({ status: 'running' });
64	    try {
65	      // Reuse the create/update payload shaping so the preview runs exactly the
66	      // config (and thresholds) the saved check would — name is irrelevant here.
67	      const payload = buildCheckPayload({
68	        ...form.getFieldsValue(true),
69	        expectation_type: expectationType,
70	      });
71	      const result = await dryRunCheck(suiteId, {
72	        expectation_type: expectationType,
73	        config: payload.config,
74	        warn_threshold: payload.warn_threshold,
75	        fail_threshold: payload.fail_threshold,
76	        critical_threshold: payload.critical_threshold,
77	        table,
78	        schema,
79	      });
80	      setState({ status: 'ok', result });
81	    } catch (err) {
82	      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });
83	    }
84	  };
85	
86	  return (
87	    <Flex vertical gap={8}>
88	      <Flex gap={12} align="center">
89	        <Button onClick={run} loading={state.status === 'running'} disabled={!!disabledReason}>
90	          Dry-run preview
91	        </Button>
92	        {disabledReason && <Typography.Text type="secondary">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>}
93	      </Flex>
94	      {state.status === 'ok' && <DryRunResultView result={state.result} />}
95	      {state.status === 'error' && (
96	        <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Dry-run failed" description={state.error} />
97	      )}
98	    </Flex>
99	  );
100	}
101	
102	function DryRunResultView({ result }: { result: CheckDryRunResult }) {
103	  return (
104	    <Descriptions
105	      size="small"
106	      bordered
107	      column={1}
108	      styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}
109	      items={[
110	        {
111	          key: 'status',
112	          label: 'Result',
113	          children: (
114	            <Tag color={RESULT_STATUS_COLORS[result.status as ResultStatus]}>{result.status}</Tag>
115	          ),
116	        },
117	        {
118	          key: 'metric',
119	          label: 'Metric',
120	          children: result.metric_value === null ? '—' : result.metric_value,
121	        },
122	        {
123	          key: 'observed',
124	          label: 'Observed',
125	          children: result.observed_value ? (
126	            <Typography.Text code>{JSON.stringify(result.observed_value)}</Typography.Text>
127	          ) : (
128	            '—'
129	          ),
130	        },
131	        {
132	          key: 'expected',
133	          label: 'Expected',
134	          children: result.expected_value ? (
135	            <Typography.Text code>{JSON.stringify(result.expected_value)}</Typography.Text>
136	          ) : (
137	            '—'
138	          ),
139	        },
140	      ]}
141	    />
142	  );
143	}
144

105	    # Scoped to suites the user owns or has a share on.
106	    suites = svc.list_suites(db, user_id=current_user.id, connection_id=connection_id)
107	    return [SuiteRead.model_validate(s) for s in suites]

113	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
114	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],

117	    return SuiteRead.model_validate(suite)

121	def update_suite(

123	    payload: SuiteUpdate,
124	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
125	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],

152	# ───────────────────────── manual run trigger ──────────────────────
153	
154	
155	@router.post(
156	    "/suites/{suite_id}/run",
157	    response_model=RunRead,
158	    status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED,
159	    summary="Trigger a run of the suite",
160	)
161	def trigger_suite_run(
162	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
163	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
164	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
165	) -> RunRead:
166	    """Queue a run of the suite and dispatch it to the worker.
167	
168	    `edit` gates this (the capability ladder grants 'trigger runs' at edit). The
169	    suite's target (#215) is resolved up front so a targetless/misconfigured
170	    suite fails fast with a 422 instead of a queued→failed run the caller has to
171	    poll to discover. A broker outage marks the run `failed` (never left stuck
172	    `queued`) and surfaces 503 — the same contract as the probe endpoint.
173	    """
174	    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
175	    connection = db.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
176	    assert connection is not None  # FK is RESTRICT; a suite always has its connection
177	    # Raises SuiteTargetInvalidError (422) for a targetless / wrong-datasource target.
178	    run_target.resolve_target(connection.type, suite.target)
179	
180	    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status="queued", triggered_by=f"manual:{current_user.id}")
181	    db.add(run)
182	    db.commit()
183	    db.refresh(run)
184	
185	    try:
186	        run_dispatch.dispatch_run(run.id)
187	    except Exception as exc:  # broker unreachable — don't leave the run stuck queued
188	        # Mark with the canonical terminal-failed shape — finished_at set,
189	        # started_at NULL (it never started) — matching the pipeline-trigger
190	        # dispatch-failure path (orchestration_service._trigger_suites) so
191	        # run-history / duration views stay consistent across trigger paths.
192	        run.status = "failed"
193	        run.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
194	        db.commit()
195	        raise HTTPException(
196	            status_code=status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
197	            detail="failed to dispatch run",
198	        ) from exc
199	    return RunRead.model_validate(run)
200	
201	
202	# ───────────────────────── export / import (portable documents) ─────

205	class CheckDocument(BaseModel):
206	    """One check inside a portable suite document — authoring fields only."""
207	
208	    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=256)
209	    kind: str = "expectation"

219	    response and the import payload (a round-trippable document)."""
220

222	    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)

224	    checks: list[CheckDocument] = Field(default_factory=list)

256	) -> SuiteRead:

268	    )

274	
275	class ColumnProfileRequest(BaseModel):
276	    columns: list[str] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=50)
277	    top_n: int = Field(default=10, ge=1, le=100, description="Most-frequent values per column")
278	    # SQL datasources: the target is a table (+ schema; Unity Catalog also catalog).
279	    table: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255, description="SQL table to profile")
280	    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="schema")
281	    catalog: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255, description="Unity Catalog catalog")
282	    # Flat-file datasources (ADLS Gen2 / S3): the target is a file path.
283	    path: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024, description="Flat-file path to profile")
284	    file_format: Literal["csv", "parquet"] | None = None
285

288	    value: Any | None
289	    count: int

293	    column: str
294	    null_count: int

296	    distinct_count: int | None

302	class ProfileRead(BaseModel):

304	    `table` / `schema` (+ `catalog` for Unity Catalog), flat-file datasources fill
305	    `path` / `file_format`."""
306	
307	    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

341	        catalog=payload.catalog,
342	        path=payload.path,
343	        file_format=payload.file_format,
344	        secret_store=secret_store,
345	    )
346	    return ProfileRead(

348	        table=result.table,
349	        schema_=result.schema,
350	        catalog=result.catalog,

352	        file_format=result.file_format,

361	                top_values=[TopValue(value=t["value"], count=t["count"]) for t in c.top_values],
362	            )

25	export function CheckNew() {

38

40	  const spec = expectationType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[expectationType] : undefined;
41	
42	  // Start the config form clean each time an expectation is (re)picked — after
43	  // the <Form> mounts (it only renders in the config step), so the store is
44	  // connected and a re-pick can't leak the prior expectation's fields.
45	  useEffect(() => {
46	    if (expectationType) form.resetFields();
47	  }, [expectationType, form]);
48

130	            </Card>
131	          ))}
132	        </Flex>
133	      </Flex>
134	    );
135	  }
136	
137	  // Step 1 — pick a category.
138	  return (

141	      <Flex wrap gap={12}>

4	import { type Check, updateCheck } from '../../api/suites';

6	import { ConfigFieldItem, SeverityThresholdFields } from './checkFormFields';

8	import { EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE, EXPECTATIONS_BY_CATEGORY } from './expectationCatalog';

10	/**
11	 * Edit a GX check. The expectation Select (grouped by category) drives which
12	 * config fields render (from the expectation catalog); the submitted `config` is
13	 * rebuilt from only the selected expectation's declared fields, so switching
14	 * types never leaks stale kwargs. Creating a check is the dedicated
15	 * `/suites/:suiteId/checks/new` page, not this drawer.
16	 */
17	export function CheckDrawer({
18	  open,
19	  suiteId,
20	  check,
21	  target,
22	  onClose,
23	  onSaved,
24	}: {
25	  open: boolean;
26	  suiteId: string;
27	  check?: Check;
28	  /** The suite's run target (#215) — drives the dry-run preview's table/schema. */
29	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
30	  onClose: () => void;
31	  onSaved: () => void;
32	}) {
33	  const { message } = App.useApp();
34	  const [form] = Form.useForm();
35	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
36	  const selectedType = Form.useWatch('expectation_type', form) as string | undefined;
37	  const spec = selectedType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[selectedType] : undefined;
38	
39	  // Reset first (antd keeps values for unmounted fields, so stale config can
40	  // survive an open→close→open with a different check), then prefill.
41	  useEffect(() => {
42	    if (!open || !check) return;
43	    form.resetFields();
44	    form.setFieldsValue({
45	      name: check.name,
46	      expectation_type: check.expectation_type,
47	      config: configToForm(EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[check.expectation_type], check.config),
48	      warn_threshold: check.warn_threshold ?? undefined,
49	      fail_threshold: check.fail_threshold ?? undefined,
50	      critical_threshold: check.critical_threshold ?? undefined,
51	    });
52	  }, [open, check, form]);
53	
54	  const onSubmit = async () => {
55	    if (!check) return;
56	    let values: Record<string, unknown>;
57	    try {
58	      values = await form.validateFields();
59	    } catch {
60	      return; // inline validation errors
61	    }
62	    const payload = buildCheckPayload(values);
63	    setSubmitting(true);
64	    try {
65	      await updateCheck(suiteId, check.id, payload);
66	      message.success(`${payload.name}: saved`);
67	      onSaved();
68	    } catch (err) {
69	      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
70	    } finally {
71	      setSubmitting(false);
72	    }
73	  };
74	
75	  return (
76	    <Drawer
77	      title={check ? `Edit “${check.name}”` : 'Edit check'}
78	      open={open}
79	      onClose={onClose}
80	      width={520}
81	      destroyOnHidden
82	      extra={
83	        <Flex gap={8}>
84	          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
85	          <Button type="primary" loading={submitting} onClick={onSubmit}>
86	            Save
87	          </Button>
88	        </Flex>
89	      }
90	    >
91	      <Form form={form} layout="vertical">
92	        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
93	          <Input placeholder="e.g. order_id not null" />
94	        </Form.Item>
95	        <Form.Item name="expectation_type" label="Expectation" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
96	          <Select
97	            placeholder="Select an expectation"
98	            // Grouped by category (antd optgroups) — the GX-Cloud-style picker.
99	            options={EXPECTATIONS_BY_CATEGORY.map((g) => ({
100	              label: g.category,
101	              options: g.specs.map((e) => ({ value: e.type, label: e.label })),
102	            }))}
103	          />
104	        </Form.Item>
105	
106	        {spec && (
107	          <>
108	            <Typography.Paragraph type="secondary" style={{ marginTop: -8 }}>
109	              {spec.description}
110	            </Typography.Paragraph>
111	            {spec.fields.map((field) => (
112	              <ConfigFieldItem key={field.name} field={field} />
113	            ))}
114	          </>
115	        )}
116	
117	        <SeverityThresholdFields />
118	
119	        <DryRunPreview
120	          suiteId={suiteId}
121	          expectationType={selectedType}
122	          target={target}
123	          form={form}
124	        />
125	      </Form>

1	import type { CheckCreate } from '../../api/suites';
2	import { EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE, type ExpectationSpec } from './expectationCatalog';
3	
4	/**
5	 * Pure check-authoring form helpers shared by the edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`)
6	 * and the dedicated create page (`CheckNew`): the form↔payload conversions, so
7	 * the two surfaces can't drift on kwarg shaping. The matching field components
8	 * live in `checkFormFields.tsx`.
9	 */
10	
11	/** Split a comma-separated list field into trimmed, non-empty items. */
12	export function parseList(value: unknown): string[] {
13	  return String(value ?? '')
14	    .split(',')
15	    .map((s) => s.trim())
16	    .filter(Boolean);
17	}
18	
19	function numOrNull(v: unknown): number | null {
20	  return typeof v === 'number' ? v : null;
21	}
22	
23	/** Build the GX `config` kwargs from only the selected expectation's fields. */
24	function formToConfig(
25	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
26	  raw: Record<string, unknown>,
27	): Record<string, unknown> {
28	  const config: Record<string, unknown> = {};
29	  if (!spec) return config;
30	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
31	    const value = raw[field.name];
32	    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') continue;
33	    if (field.type === 'list') {
34	      const items = parseList(value);
35	      if (items.length > 0) config[field.name] = items;
36	    } else {
37	      config[field.name] = value;
38	    }
39	  }
40	  return config;
41	}
42	
43	/** Inverse of formToConfig for edit-mode prefill (list array → comma string). */
44	export function configToForm(
45	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
46	  config: Record<string, unknown>,
47	): Record<string, unknown> {
48	  const form: Record<string, unknown> = {};
49	  if (!spec) return form;
50	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
51	    const value = config[field.name];
52	    if (value === undefined) continue;
53	    form[field.name] = field.type === 'list' && Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value;
54	  }
55	  return form;
56	}
57	
58	/** Assemble the create/update payload from validated form values. Rebuilds
59	 *  `config` from only the selected expectation's fields, so switching types
60	 *  never leaks stale kwargs. */
61	export function buildCheckPayload(values: Record<string, unknown>): CheckCreate {
62	  const spec = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[values.expectation_type as string];
63	  return {
64	    name: values.name as string,
65	    expectation_type: values.expectation_type as string,
66	    config: formToConfig(spec, (values.config ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>),
67	    warn_threshold: numOrNull(values.warn_threshold),
68	    fail_threshold: numOrNull(values.fail_threshold),
69	    critical_threshold: numOrNull(values.critical_threshold),
70	  };
71	}
72

4	 * The backend treats `expectation_type` as a snake_case string (title-cased to a
5	 * GX expectation class) and `config` as free-form GX kwargs — there is no server
6	 * catalog. This file is the frontend's single source of truth for which
7	 * expectations are offered and what typed config each needs, the same spec-driven
8	 * idiom as `connectionFormSpec.ts`.

1	import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
2	
3	/** Three-state result of an async fetch. */
4	export type AsyncState<T> =
5	  | { status: 'loading' }
6	  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }
7	  | { status: 'error'; error: string };
8	
9	/**
10	 * Fetch on mount (and on `reload()`), with a cancelled-guard so a late
11	 * resolution after unmount doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a
12	 * string `error`. Shared by the data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the
13	 * cancelled-effect dance lives in one place rather than being re-derived per page.
14	 *
15	 * `reload` re-runs the fetcher (e.g. after a mutation) while keeping the current
16	 * data visible until the refetch resolves — no flash back to the loading state.
17	 */
18	export function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): {
19	  state: AsyncState<T>;
20	  reload: () => void;
21	} {
22	  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });
23	  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    let cancelled = false;
27	    fetcher()
28	      .then((data) => {
29	        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
30	      })
31	      .catch((err: unknown) => {
32	        if (!cancelled) {
33	          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
34	        }
35	      });
36	    return () => {
37	      cancelled = true;
38	    };
39	    // Re-run on mount and whenever `reload` bumps the nonce; the fetcher identity
40	    // is intentionally not a dependency.
41	    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
42	  }, [nonce]);
43	
44	  const reload = useCallback(() => setNonce((n) => n + 1), []);
45	  return { state, reload };
46	}
47

'');\n  const [prevColumn, setPrevColumn] = useState(column);\n  if (column !== prevColumn) {\n    setPrevColumn(column);\n    if (column) setValue(column);\n  }\n\n  const [state, setState] = useState<\n    | { status: 'idle' }\n    | { status: 'running' }\n    | { status: 'ok'; result: ProfileResult }\n    | { status: 'error'; error: string }\n  >({ status: 'idle' });\n\n  const disabledReason = !profileTarget\n    ? 'Set a table or file target on the suite to profile.'\n    : !value.trim()\n      ? 'Enter a column to profile.'\n      : undefined;\n\n  const run = async () => {\n    if (!profileTarget || !value.trim()) return;\n    setState({ status: 'running' });\n    try {\n      const result = await profileColumns(suiteId, {\n        columns: [value.trim()],\n        ...profileTarget,\n      });\n      setState({ status: 'ok', result });\n    } catch (err) {\n      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Collapse\n      size=\"small\"\n      items={[\n        {\n          key: 'profiler',\n          label: 'Column profiler',\n          children: (\n            <Flex vertical gap={8}>\n              <Flex gap={8} align=\"center\" wrap>\n                <Input\n                  value={value}\n                  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}\n                  placeholder=\"Column to profile\"\n                  style={{ maxWidth: 240 }}\n                  onPressEnter={run}\n                />\n                <Button\n                  onClick={run}\n                  loading={state.status === 'running'}\n                  disabled={!!disabledReason}\n                >\n                  Profile\n                </Button>\n                {disabledReason && (\n                  <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>\n                )}\n              </Flex>\n              {state.status === 'ok' && <ProfileView result={state.result} />}\n              {state.status === 'error' && (\n                <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message=\"Profile failed\" description={state.error} />\n              )}\n            </Flex>\n          ),\n        },\n      ]}\n    />\n  );\n}\n\n/** Pull the datasource-shaped identity out of the suite target, or null when no\n *  profilable target is set (the backend needs a `table` or a `path`). */\nfunction extractProfileTarget(\n  target: Record<string, unknown> | null,\n): Pick<\n  import('../../api/suites').ColumnProfileRequest,\n  'table' | 'schema' | 'catalog' | 'path' | 'file_format'\n> | null {\n  if (!target) return null;\n  const str = (k: string): string | undefined =>\n    typeof target[k] === 'string' ? (target[k] as string) : undefined;\n  const table = str('table');\n  const path = str('path');\n  if (!table && !path) return null;\n  return {\n    table,\n    schema: str('schema'),\n    catalog: str('catalog'),\n    path,\n    file_format: str('file_format') as 'csv' | 'parquet' | undefined,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction renderScalar(v: unknown): string {\n  if (v === null || v === undefined) return '—';\n  return typeof v === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(v) : String(v);\n}\n\nfunction ProfileView({ result }: { result: ProfileResult }) {\n  const col: ColumnProfile | undefined = result.columns[0];\n  if (!col) return null;\n  const nullPct = (col.null_fraction * 100).toFixed(1);\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={8}>\n      <Descriptions\n        size=\"small\"\n        bordered\n        column={1}\n        styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}\n        items={[\n          { key: 'column', label: 'Column', children: col.column },\n          { key: 'rows', label: 'Row count', children: result.row_count },\n          {\n            key: 'nulls',\n            label: 'Nulls',\n            children: `${col.null_count} (${nullPct}%)`,\n          },\n          {\n            key: 'distinct',\n            label: 'Distinct',\n            children: col.distinct_count === null ? '—' : col.distinct_count,\n          },\n          { key: 'min', label: 'Min', children: renderScalar(col.min_value) },\n          { key: 'max', label: 'Max', children: renderScalar(col.max_value) },\n        ]}\n      />\n      {col.top_values.length > 0 && (\n        <Table\n          size=\"small\"\n          pagination={false}\n          rowKey={(_, i) => String(i)}\n          dataSource={col.top_values}\n          columns={[\n            { title: 'Top value', dataIndex: 'value', render: (v: unknown) => renderScalar(v) },\n            { title: 'Count', dataIndex: 'count', width: 100 },\n          ]}\n        />\n      )}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n"
}

diff --git a/frontend/src/components/checks/ColumnProfilePanel.tsx b/frontend/src/components/checks/ColumnProfilePanel.tsx
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c2cddca
--- /dev/null
+++ b/frontend/src/components/checks/ColumnProfilePanel.tsx
@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+import { Alert, Button, Collapse, Descriptions, Flex, Input, Table, Typography } from 'antd';
+import { useState } from 'react';
+
+import {
+  type ColumnProfile,
+  type ColumnProfileRequest,
+  profileColumns,
+  type ProfileResult,
+} from '../../api/suites';
+
+/**
+ * Inline column-profiler panel for the check editor: profiles one column of the
+ * suite's run target (#215) — nulls, distinct count, min/max, top values — so
+ * the author can ground a check's config (a value range, an allowed set, a null
+ * threshold) in the real data before saving. Reads-only, persists nothing
+ * (`POST /suites/{id}/profile`). Shared by the create page (`CheckNew`) and the
+ * edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`).
+ *
+ * The profiled column pre-fills from the check's `column` config field (so
+ * picking a column for the expectation primes the profiler), but stays editable
+ * so the author can explore neighbouring columns. Collapsed by default to keep
+ * the editor uncluttered — it's an opt-in aid, not always-on.
+ *
+ * Backend limits surface as the API's error message (e.g. no credential,
+ * unreachable warehouse); the button is disabled with a reason until the suite
+ * has a table/file target and a column is entered.
+ */
+export function ColumnProfilePanel({
+  suiteId,
+  target,
+  column,
+}: {
+  suiteId: string;
+  /** The suite's run target (#215) — supplies the table/file identity. */
+  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
+  /** The check's currently-selected column, used to pre-fill the input. */
+  column: string | undefined;
+}) {
+  const profileTarget = extractProfileTarget(target);
+
+  // Pre-fill from the check's column, but let the author override. Render-phase
+  // sync (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern) so picking the
+  // expectation's column primes the input without an effect round-trip.
+  const [value, setValue] = useState(column ?? '');
+  const [prevColumn, setPrevColumn] = useState(column);
+  if (column !== prevColumn) {
+    setPrevColumn(column);
+    if (column) setValue(column);
+  }
+
+  const [state, setState] = useState<
+    | { status: 'idle' }
+    | { status: 'running' }
+    | { status: 'ok'; result: ProfileResult }
+    | { status: 'error'; error: string }
+  >({ status: 'idle' });
+
+  const disabledReason = !profileTarget
+    ? 'Set a table or file target on the suite to profile.'
+    : !value.trim()
+      ? 'Enter a column to profile.'
+      : undefined;
+
+  const run = async () => {
+    if (!profileTarget || !value.trim()) return;
+    setState({ status: 'running' });
+    try {
+      const result = await profileColumns(suiteId, {
+        columns: [value.trim()],
+        ...profileTarget,
+      });
+      setState({ status: 'ok', result });
+    } catch (err) {
+      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });
+    }
+  };
+
+  return (
+    <Collapse
+      size="small"
+      items={[
+        {
+          key: 'profiler',
+          label: 'Column profiler',
+          children: (
+            <Flex vertical gap={8}>
+              <Flex gap={8} align="center" wrap>
+                <Input
+                  value={value}
+                  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
+                  placeholder="Column to profile"
+                  style={{ maxWidth: 240 }}
+                  onPressEnter={run}
+                />
+                <Button
+                  onClick={run}
+                  loading={state.status === 'running'}
+                  disabled={!!disabledReason}
+                >
+                  Profile
+                </Button>
+                {disabledReason && (
+                  <Typography.Text type="secondary">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>
+                )}
+              </Flex>
+              {state.status === 'ok' && <ProfileView result={state.result} />}
+              {state.status === 'error' && (
+                <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Profile failed" description={state.error} />
+              )}
+            </Flex>
+          ),
+        },
+      ]}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+/** Pull the datasource-shaped identity out of the suite target, or null when no
+ *  profilable target is set (the backend needs a `table` or a `path`). */
+function extractProfileTarget(
+  target: Record<string, unknown> | null,
+): Pick<ColumnProfileRequest, 'table' | 'schema' | 'catalog' | 'path' | 'file_format'> | null {
+  if (!target) return null;
+  const str = (k: string): string | undefined =>
+    typeof target[k] === 'string' ? (target[k] as string) : undefined;
+  const table = str('table');
+  const path = str('path');
+  if (!table && !path) return null;
+  return {
+    table,
+    schema: str('schema'),
+    catalog: str('catalog'),
+    path,
+    file_format: str('file_format') as 'csv' | 'parquet' | undefined,
+  };
+}
+
+function renderScalar(v: unknown): string {
+  if (v === null || v === undefined) return '—';
+  return typeof v === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(v) : String(v);
+}
+
+function ProfileView({ result }: { result: ProfileResult }) {
+  const col: ColumnProfile | undefined = result.columns[0];
+  if (!col) return null;
+  const nullPct = (col.null_fraction * 100).toFixed(1);
+  return (
+    <Flex vertical gap={8}>
+      <Descriptions
+        size="small"
+        bordered
+        column={1}
+        styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}
+        items={[
+          { key: 'column', label: 'Column', children: col.column },
+          { key: 'rows', label: 'Row count', children: result.row_count },
+          {
+            key: 'nulls',
+            label: 'Nulls',
+            children: `${col.null_count} (${nullPct}%)`,
+          },
+          {
+            key: 'distinct',
+            label: 'Distinct',
+            children: col.distinct_count === null ? '—' : col.distinct_count,
+          },
+          { key: 'min', label: 'Min', children: renderScalar(col.min_value) },
+          { key: 'max', label: 'Max', children: renderScalar(col.max_value) },
+        ]}
+      />
+      {col.top_values.length > 0 && (
+        <Table
+          size="small"
+          pagination={false}
+          rowKey={(_, i) => String(i)}
+          dataSource={col.top_values}
+          columns={[
+            { title: 'Top value', dataIndex: 'value', render: (v: unknown) => renderScalar(v) },
+            { title: 'Count', dataIndex: 'count', width: 100 },
+          ]}
+        />
+      )}
+    </Flex>
+  );
+}

The `column` config field name matches the watch path. The pre-fill works for column-scoped expectations.

I've thoroughly reviewed all three angles. The contract between the panel and backend holds: the frontend sends key `schema` (the alias), and Pydantic v2 accepts input by alias by default even without `populate_by_name` — so that is NOT a bug. The `CheckNew` fragment wrapping preserves prior behavior. No null-deref, falsy-zero, missing-await, or swallowed-error bugs found in the component logic.

[]

No confirmed or plausible correctness bugs found.

Notes on the specific concerns raised:

- **`schema` field alias / `populate_by_name`**: Not a bug. The frontend sends the JSON key `schema` (both `extractProfileTarget` and the `ColumnProfileRequest` TS interface use `schema`). The backend field is `schema_ = Field(alias="schema")` without `populate_by_name=True`, but in Pydantic v2 the alias is the input key by default — so `schema` is exactly what's accepted. (Sending `schema_` would have failed; the panel correctly sends `schema`.) The suite `target` JSONB is also stored under `schema` via `SuiteTarget.to_storage()`'s `by_alias=True`, so `extractProfileTarget`'s `target['schema']` read lines up.

- **Request body shape**: Accepted. Body is `{ columns: [trimmed], table?, schema?, catalog?, path?, file_format? }`. `top_n` is omitted but has a backend default (`10`), and absent identity fields are `undefined` (dropped from JSON), satisfying the optional/nullable backend fields. `columns` has exactly one trimmed entry, meeting `min_length=1`.

- **CheckNew fragment change**: Behavior-preserving. The single `<Form.Item><DryRunPreview/></Form.Item>` was replaced by a fragment holding two sibling `Form.Item`s (profiler + dry-run), still gated by `suiteId &&`. No invariant dropped.

- **Render-phase column sync**: Correct. When `column` becomes `undefined` (field cleared), `prevColumn` updates but `value` is intentionally retained (`if (column) setValue(column)`), matching the documented "editable, pre-fill only on a real column" intent — not a falsy bug.

- **Error handling / await**: `run` awaits `profileColumns` and catches, surfacing `err.message`; no swallowed errors. The `!value.trim()` / `!profileTarget` guards and `disabledReason` use truthy string checks (no numeric-zero hazard since these are strings).

30	  switch (status) {
31	    case 'succeeded':
32	      return 'success';
33	    case 'failed':
34	      return 'error';
35	    case 'running':

44	/** Absolute timestamp as a locale string, or an em dash when absent. */
45	export function formatTimestamp(iso: string | null): string {
46	  if (!iso) return '—';
47	  const d = new Date(iso);
48	  return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? '—' : d.toLocaleString();
49	}
50	
51	/**
52	 * Run duration (finished − started) as a compact human string: `850ms`, `12s`,
53	 * `1m 3s`. Returns an em dash when either bound is missing (queued / never
54	 * finished) or the interval is negative (clock skew).
55	 */
56	export function formatDuration(startedAt: string | null, finishedAt: string | null): string {
57	  if (!startedAt || !finishedAt) return '—';
58	  const ms = new Date(finishedAt).getTime() - new Date(startedAt).getTime();
59	  if (Number.isNaN(ms) || ms < 0) return '—';
60	  if (ms < 1000) return `${ms}ms`;
61	  const totalSeconds = Math.round(ms / 1000);
62	  if (totalSeconds < 60) return `${totalSeconds}s`;
63	  const minutes = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 60);
64	  const seconds = totalSeconds % 60;
65	  return `${minutes}m ${seconds}s`;
66	}

Done. Picked up and shipped the next Week-4 item: the **inline column-profiler panel** in the check editor.

## What landed — PR [#232](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/232)

`ColumnProfilePanel` — a collapsed-by-default panel shared by the create page ([CheckNew.tsx](frontend/src/pages/CheckNew.tsx)) and the edit drawer ([CheckDrawer.tsx](frontend/src/components/checks/CheckDrawer.tsx)). It profiles one column of the suite's run target (#215) via the existing `POST /suites/{id}/profile` (no persistence) and renders null count/fraction, distinct count, min/max, and top values — so an author can ground a range / allowed-set / null threshold in real data before saving.

Key behaviours:
- Column **pre-fills from the check's `column` config field** (render-phase prop-sync, same idiom as `DryRunPreview`) but stays editable.
- Target identity (`table`/`schema`/`catalog` for SQL, `path`/`file_format` for flat files) is pulled from the suite target.
- Disabled-with-reason until target + column present; backend limits surface as a clean error alert.
- Extracted `formatScalar` into the shared [resultsFormat.ts](frontend/src/components/results/resultsFormat.ts) and consumed it (renders falsy scalars `0`/`false`/`''` correctly, not as the em dash).

## Process
- **Review:** dispatched two review agents (correctness + cleanup) rather than self-review. Correctness found nothing (the `schema`-alias contract checks out). Cleanup found two reuse items — I applied the `formatScalar` extraction here and filed the broader migration (DryRunPreview/Results + a shared target extractor) as **[#231](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/231)** so nothing's silently dropped.
- **Verified locally:** 72 tests green, `tsc`/`eslint`/`prettier`/`vite build` all clean.
- **Docs:** updated [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md) (Check editor UI 5/9, Week 4 18/26) and CLAUDE.md §13 headline.

Live warehouse/file profiling stays the deferred smoke (no DEV creds), consistent with the rest of the run path. CI is running on the PR now.

title:	Frontend cleanup: share run-target string extraction + migrate DryRunPreview/Results onto formatScalar
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	231
--
Two reuse cleanups surfaced by the `/code-review` of the column-profiler panel PR (PR-D2). Both are low-risk and touch already-shipped components, so deferred out of that PR to keep it focused.

### 1. Migrate `DryRunPreview` + `Results` onto the shared `formatScalar`
PR-D2 extracted `formatScalar(value)` into `frontend/src/components/results/resultsFormat.ts` (em dash for null/undefined, `JSON.stringify` for objects, `String` otherwise) and `ColumnProfilePanel` consumes it. The same scalar/JSON rendering is still hand-rolled inline in:
- `frontend/src/components/checks/DryRunPreview.tsx` (observed/expected value rendering) — note its `result.observed_value ? ... : '—'` currently collapses a falsy scalar (e.g. `0`, `false`) to the em dash; `formatScalar` fixes that.
- `frontend/src/components/results/Results.tsx` (~line 223, per-check observed value).

Migrating both onto `formatScalar` removes the duplication and closes the latent falsy-value display gap in `DryRunPreview`. Watch the existing `DryRunPreview`/`Results` tests when changing the falsy-value behaviour.

### 2. Share the suite run-target string extraction
`ColumnProfilePanel.extractProfileTarget` and `DryRunPreview` (the `typeof target?.table === 'string' ? ... : undefined` reads) both pull the #215 run-target identity out of the same untyped `Record<string, unknown>` bag. A shared `targetString(target, key)` helper — or a typed `RunTarget` interface at the #215 source (`api/suites.ts` `Suite.target`) — would keep them from drifting as flat-file/UC targets fill out.

_Source: code-review of `feature/check-editor-column-profiler-panel`._

9	/**
10	 * Inline "preview before saving" affordance for the check editor: runs the
11	 * in-progress check against the suite's live target via the dry-run API
12	 * (`POST /suites/{id}/checks/dryrun`) and shows the severity outcome — without
13	 * persisting a Run/Result. Shared by the create page (`CheckNew`) and the edit
14	 * drawer (`CheckDrawer`); both pass the suite's run target (#215) so the same
15	 * `table`/`schema` the run would use is previewed.
16	 *
17	 * v1 backend limits (surfaced as the API's error message): dry-run needs a
18	 * table target and a Snowflake connection. The button is disabled (with a
19	 * reason) until an expectation is picked and the suite has a table target;
20	 * everything else (no credential, unreachable warehouse, wrong datasource) comes
21	 * back as a clean error from the API and renders in the alert.
22	 */
23	export function DryRunPreview({
24	  suiteId,
25	  expectationType,
26	  target,
27	  form,
28	}: {
29	  suiteId: string;
30	  expectationType: string | undefined;
31	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
32	  form: FormInstance;
33	}) {
34	  const [state, setState] = useState<
35	    | { status: 'idle' }
36	    | { status: 'running' }
37	    | { status: 'ok'; result: CheckDryRunResult }
38	    | { status: 'error'; error: string }
39	  >({ status: 'idle' });
40	
41	  // Clear a previous preview when the expectation changes — in the edit drawer
42	  // the picker switches type in-place (DryRunPreview stays mounted), so without
43	  // this the old result would linger, misattributed to the new expectation.
44	  // Render-phase reset (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern)
45	  // rather than an effect, so the stale result never paints.
46	  const [prevExpectation, setPrevExpectation] = useState(expectationType);
47	  if (expectationType !== prevExpectation) {
48	    setPrevExpectation(expectationType);
49	    setState({ status: 'idle' });
50	  }
51	
52	  const table = typeof target?.table === 'string' ? target.table : undefined;
53	  const schema = typeof target?.schema === 'string' ? target.schema : null;
54	
55	  const disabledReason = !expectationType
56	    ? 'Pick an expectation to preview it.'
57	    : !table
58	      ? 'Set a table target on the suite to preview against live data.'
59	      : undefined;
60	
61	  const run = async () => {
62	    if (!expectationType || !table) return;
63	    setState({ status: 'running' });
64	    try {
65	      // Reuse the create/update payload shaping so the preview runs exactly the
66	      // config (and thresholds) the saved check would — name is irrelevant here.
67	      const payload = buildCheckPayload({
68	        ...form.getFieldsValue(true),
69	        expectation_type: expectationType,
70	      });
71	      const result = await dryRunCheck(suiteId, {
72	        expectation_type: expectationType,
73	        config: payload.config,
74	        warn_threshold: payload.warn_threshold,
75	        fail_threshold: payload.fail_threshold,
76	        critical_threshold: payload.critical_threshold,
77	        table,
78	        schema,
79	      });
80	      setState({ status: 'ok', result });
81	    } catch (err) {
82	      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });
83	    }
84	  };
85	
86	  return (
87	    <Flex vertical gap={8}>
88	      <Flex gap={12} align="center">
89	        <Button onClick={run} loading={state.status === 'running'} disabled={!!disabledReason}>
90	          Dry-run preview
91	        </Button>
92	        {disabledReason && <Typography.Text type="secondary">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>}
93	      </Flex>
94	      {state.status === 'ok' && <DryRunResultView result={state.result} />}
95	      {state.status === 'error' && (
96	        <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Dry-run failed" description={state.error} />
97	      )}
98	    </Flex>
99	  );
100	}
101	
102	function DryRunResultView({ result }: { result: CheckDryRunResult }) {
103	  return (
104	    <Descriptions
105	      size="small"
106	      bordered
107	      column={1}
108	      styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}
109	      items={[
110	        {
111	          key: 'status',
112	          label: 'Result',
113	          children: (
114	            <Tag color={RESULT_STATUS_COLORS[result.status as ResultStatus]}>{result.status}</Tag>
115	          ),
116	        },
117	        {
118	          key: 'metric',

121	        },

20	  pass: 'success',
21	  warn: 'warning',
22	  fail: 'error',
23	  critical: 'magenta',
24	  skip: 'default',
25	  error: 'volcano',
26	};
27	
28	/** Orchestrator pipeline-run status → colour (provider-agnostic value set). */
29	export function pipelineStatusColor(status: string): string {
30	  switch (status) {
31	    case 'succeeded':
32	      return 'success';
33	    case 'failed':
34	      return 'error';
35	    case 'running':
36	      return 'processing';
37	    case 'cancelled':
38	      return 'warning';
39	    default:
40	      return 'default';
41	  }
42	}
43	
44	/**
45	 * Render an unknown scalar (a GX observed/expected value, a profiled min/max or
46	 * top value) for display: an em dash for null/undefined, JSON for objects, the
47	 * `String` form otherwise. Falsy scalars (`0`, `false`, `''`) render as
48	 * themselves — not collapsed to the em dash — so a real zero isn't mistaken for
49	 * "no value". The em-dash sentinel matches `formatTimestamp` / `formatDuration`.
50	 */
51	export function formatScalar(value: unknown): string {
52	  if (value === null || value === undefined) return '—';
53	  return typeof value === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(value) : String(value);
54	}
55	
56	/** Absolute timestamp as a locale string, or an em dash when absent. */
57	export function formatTimestamp(iso: string | null): string {
58	  if (!iso) return '—';
59	  const d = new Date(iso);
60	  return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? '—' : d.toLocaleString();
61	}
62	
63	/**
64	 * Run duration (finished − started) as a compact human string: `850ms`, `12s`,
65	 * `1m 3s`. Returns an em dash when either bound is missing (queued / never
66	 * finished) or the interval is negative (clock skew).
67	 */
68	export function formatDuration(startedAt: string | null, finishedAt: string | null): string {
69	  if (!startedAt || !finishedAt) return '—';
70	  const ms = new Date(finishedAt).getTime() - new Date(startedAt).getTime();
71	  if (Number.isNaN(ms) || ms < 0) return '—';
72	  if (ms < 1000) return `${ms}ms`;
73	  const totalSeconds = Math.round(ms / 1000);
74	  if (totalSeconds < 60) return `${totalSeconds}s`;
75	  const minutes = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 60);
76	  const seconds = totalSeconds % 60;
77	  return `${minutes}m ${seconds}s`;
78	}

4	import {
5	  type ColumnProfile,
6	  type ColumnProfileRequest,
7	  profileColumns,
8	  type ProfileResult,
9	} from '../../api/suites';
10	import { formatScalar } from '../results/resultsFormat';
11	
12	/**
13	 * Inline column-profiler panel for the check editor: profiles one column of the
14	 * suite's run target (#215) — nulls, distinct count, min/max, top values — so
15	 * the author can ground a check's config (a value range, an allowed set, a null
16	 * threshold) in the real data before saving. Reads-only, persists nothing
17	 * (`POST /suites/{id}/profile`). Shared by the create page (`CheckNew`) and the
18	 * edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`).
19	 *
20	 * The profiled column pre-fills from the check's `column` config field (so
21	 * picking a column for the expectation primes the profiler), but stays editable
22	 * so the author can explore neighbouring columns. Collapsed by default to keep
23	 * the editor uncluttered — it's an opt-in aid, not always-on.
24	 *
25	 * Backend limits surface as the API's error message (e.g. no credential,
26	 * unreachable warehouse); the button is disabled with a reason until the suite
27	 * has a table/file target and a column is entered.
28	 */
29	export function ColumnProfilePanel({
30	  suiteId,
31	  target,
32	  column,
33	}: {
34	  suiteId: string;
35	  /** The suite's run target (#215) — supplies the table/file identity. */
36	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
37	  /** The check's currently-selected column, used to pre-fill the input. */
38	  column: string | undefined;
39	}) {
40	  const profileTarget = extractProfileTarget(target);
41	
42	  // Pre-fill from the check's column, but let the author override. Render-phase
43	  // sync (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern) so picking the
44	  // expectation's column primes the input without an effect round-trip.
45	  const [value, setValue] = useState(column ?? '');
46	  const [prevColumn, setPrevColumn] = useState(column);
47	  if (column !== prevColumn) {
48	    setPrevColumn(column);
49	    if (column) setValue(column);
50	  }
51	
52	  const [state, setState] = useState<
53	    | { status: 'idle' }
54	    | { status: 'running' }
55	    | { status: 'ok'; result: ProfileResult }
56	    | { status: 'error'; error: string }
57	  >({ status: 'idle' });
58	
59	  const disabledReason = !profileTarget
60	    ? 'Set a table or file target on the suite to profile.'
61	    : !value.trim()
62	      ? 'Enter a column to profile.'
63	      : undefined;
64	
65	  const run = async () => {
66	    if (!profileTarget || !value.trim()) return;
67	    setState({ status: 'running' });
68	    try {
69	      const result = await profileColumns(suiteId, {
70	        columns: [value.trim()],
71	        ...profileTarget,
72	      });
73	      setState({ status: 'ok', result });
74	    } catch (err) {
75	      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });
76	    }
77	  };
78	
79	  return (
80	    <Collapse
81	      size="small"
82	      items={[
83	        {
84	          key: 'profiler',
85	          label: 'Column profiler',
86	          children: (
87	            <Flex vertical gap={8}>
88	              <Flex gap={8} align="center" wrap>
89	                <Input
90	                  value={value}
91	                  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
92	                  placeholder="Column to profile"
93	                  style={{ maxWidth: 240 }}
94	                  onPressEnter={run}
95	                />
96	                <Button
97	                  onClick={run}
98	                  loading={state.status === 'running'}
99	                  disabled={!!disabledReason}
100	                >
101	                  Profile
102	                </Button>
103	                {disabledReason && (
104	                  <Typography.Text type="secondary">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>
105	                )}
106	              </Flex>
107	              {state.status === 'ok' && <ProfileView result={state.result} />}
108	              {state.status === 'error' && (
109	                <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Profile failed" description={state.error} />
110	              )}
111	            </Flex>
112	          ),
113	        },
114	      ]}
115	    />
116	  );
117	}
118	
119	/** Pull the datasource-shaped identity out of the suite target, or null when no
120	 *  profilable target is set (the backend needs a `table` or a `path`). */
121	function extractProfileTarget(
122	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null,
123	): Pick<ColumnProfileRequest, 'table' | 'schema' | 'catalog' | 'path' | 'file_format'> | null {
124	  if (!target) return null;
125	  const str = (k: string): string | undefined =>
126	    typeof target[k] === 'string' ? (target[k] as string) : undefined;
127	  const table = str('table');
128	  const path = str('path');
129	  if (!table && !path) return null;
130	  return {
131	    table,
132	    schema: str('schema'),
133	    catalog: str('catalog'),
134	    path,
135	    file_format: str('file_format') as 'csv' | 'parquet' | undefined,
136	  };
137	}
138	
139	function ProfileView({ result }: { result: ProfileResult }) {
140	  const col: ColumnProfile | undefined = result.columns[0];
141	  if (!col) return null;
142	  const nullPct = (col.null_fraction * 100).toFixed(1);
143	  return (
144	    <Flex vertical gap={8}>
145	      <Descriptions
146	        size="small"
147	        bordered
148	        column={1}
149	        styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}
150	        items={[
151	          { key: 'column', label: 'Column', children: col.column },
152	          { key: 'rows', label: 'Row count', children: result.row_count },
153	          {
154	            key: 'nulls',
155	            label: 'Nulls',
156	            children: `${col.null_count} (${nullPct}%)`,
157	          },
158	          {
159	            key: 'distinct',
160	            label: 'Distinct',
161	            children: col.distinct_count === null ? '—' : col.distinct_count,
162	          },
163	          { key: 'min', label: 'Min', children: formatScalar(col.min_value) },
164	          { key: 'max', label: 'Max', children: formatScalar(col.max_value) },
165	        ]}
166	      />
167	      {col.top_values.length > 0 && (
168	        <Table
169	          size="small"
170	          pagination={false}
171	          rowKey={(_, i) => String(i)}
172	          dataSource={col.top_values}
173	          columns={[
174	            { title: 'Top value', dataIndex: 'value', render: (v: unknown) => formatScalar(v) },
175	            { title: 'Count', dataIndex: 'count', width: 100 },
176	          ]}
177	        />
178	      )}
179	    </Flex>
180	  );
181	}
182

+/**
+ * The datasource-shaped identity carried in `Suite.target` (#215): SQL targets
+ * fill `table`/`schema`/`catalog`, flat-file targets fill `path`/`file_format`.
+ * The wire shape is an untyped JSONB bag (`Record<string, unknown>`); read it
+ * through `targetString` so the dry-run preview and column profiler don't each
+ * re-hand-roll the `typeof x === 'string'` extraction.
+ */
+export interface RunTarget {
+  table?: string;
+  schema?: string;
+  catalog?: string;
+  path?: string;
+  file_format?: 'csv' | 'parquet';
+}
+
+/** Read one string field out of the untyped run-target bag, or `undefined`. */
+export function targetString(
+  target: Record<string, unknown> | null,

+import { Typography } from 'antd';
+
+import { formatScalar } from './resultsFormat';
+
+/**
+ * Render a GX observed/expected value (or any unknown scalar/JSON blob) the way
+ * the Results table and the dry-run preview both want it: an em dash for
+ * null/undefined, otherwise the `formatScalar` string in a monospace `code` box.
+ * Shared so the `null ? '—' : <Text code>{JSON.stringify(...)}</Text>` pattern
+ * lives in one place (#231); `formatScalar` also renders falsy scalars (`0`,
+ * `false`, `''`) as themselves instead of collapsing them to the em dash.
+ */
+export function ScalarValue({ value }: { value: unknown }) {
+  if (value === null || value === undefined) return <>—</>;
+  return <Typography.Text code>{formatScalar(value)}</Typography.Text>;
+}

The falsy-collapse fix is latent-only given the typing, but it's a strict improvement, not a behavior break.
- `targetString` is genuinely new shared surface (no pre-existing equivalent), called at both sites; `Typography` remains used in both touched files (lint confirms). Cast `as 'csv' | 'parquet'` is carried over unchanged, not newly introduced.

# ───────────────────────── export / import (portable documents) ─────


class CheckDocument(BaseModel):
    """One check inside a portable suite document — authoring fields only."""

    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=256)
    kind: str = "expectation"
    expectation_type: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    config: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None = None
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None = None


class SuiteDocument(BaseModel):
    """Portable suite — connection-agnostic, no DB identity. Both the export
    response and the import payload (a round-trippable document)."""

    version: int = suite_io.EXPORT_VERSION
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024)
    checks: list[CheckDocument] = Field(default_factory=list)


class SuiteImportRequest(BaseModel):
    connection_id: uuid.UUID
    document: SuiteDocument


@router.get(
    "/suites/{suite_id}/export",
    response_model=SuiteDocument,
    summary="Export a suite as a portable document",
)
def export_suite(
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> SuiteDocument:
    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="view")
    return SuiteDocument.model_validate(suite_io.export_suite(suite))


@router.post(
    "/suites/import",
    response_model=SuiteRead,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    summary="Import a suite document onto a connection",
)
def import_suite(
    payload: SuiteImportRequest,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> SuiteRead:
    # Like create_suite: any authenticated user may import; the new suite is
    # owned by them. Thresholds/config round-trip exactly (Decimal in/out).
    doc = payload.document
    suite = suite_io.import_suite(
        db,
        version=doc.version,
        name=doc.name,
        description=doc.description,
        checks=[c.model_dump() for c in doc.checks],
        connection_id=payload.connection_id,
        created_by=current_user.id,
    )
    return SuiteRead.model_validate(suite)


# ───────────────────────── column profiler (no persistence) ─────────


class ColumnProfileRequest(BaseModel):
    columns: list[str] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=50)
    top_n: int = Field(default=10, ge=1, le=100, description="Most-frequent values per column")
    # SQL datasources: the target is a table (+ schema; Unity Catalog also catalog).
    table: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255, description="SQL table to profile")
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="schema")
    catalog: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=255, description="Unity Catalog catalog")
    # Flat-file datasources (ADLS Gen2 / S3): the target is a file path.
    path: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1024, description="Flat-file path to profile")
    file_format: Literal["csv", "parquet"] | None = None


class TopValue(BaseModel):
    value: Any | None
    count: int


class ColumnProfileRead(BaseModel):
    column: str
    null_count: int
    null_fraction: float
    distinct_count: int | None
    min_value: Any | None
    max_value: Any | None
    top_values: list[TopValue]


class ProfileRead(BaseModel):
    """Profile result. Identity fields are type-specific: SQL datasources fill
    `table` / `schema` (+ `catalog` for Unity Catalog), flat-file datasources fill
    `path` / `file_format`."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    row_count: int
    columns: list[ColumnProfileRead]
    table: str | None = None
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, serialization_alias="schema")
    catalog: str | None = None
    path: str | None = None
    file_format: str | None = None

=== #212 ===
create_suite accepts an orchestration connection (ADF/Airflow) as a suite target
Surfaced by the full-stack E2E smoke (#211 review).

## Problem
`suite_service.create_suite` validates only that `connection_id` references an existing connection — **not** that the connection is a *datasource*. So `POST /suites` with an ADF or Airflow `connection_id` returns **201**, binding a suite to an orchestration provider.

This violates the core boundary (CLAUDE.md §4 / §11): ADF + Airflow are orchestration providers, **not** queryable datasources — you can't author/run DQ checks against them. A suite bound to one is a semantically invalid, unrunnable state.

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/lib/download.ts",
  "content": "/**\n * Trigger a browser download of `data` serialised as pretty-printed JSON.\n *\n * Builds an object-URL blob and clicks a transient anchor — the standard\n * no-backend \"save this JSON\" path (used by the suite export). The URL is\n * revoked immediately after the click so the blob doesn't leak.\n */\nexport function downloadJson(filename: string, data: unknown): void {\n  const blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' });\n  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);\n  const anchor = document.createElement('a');\n  anchor.href = url;\n  anchor.download = filename;\n  document.body.appendChild(anchor);\n  anchor.click();\n  anchor.remove();\n  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);\n}\n\n/**\n * Turn an arbitrary label into a safe, lowercase filename stem: non-word\n * characters collapse to underscores, runs trim to one, leading/trailing\n * underscores drop. Falls back to `fallback` when nothing usable remains (e.g.\n * a name of only punctuation).\n */\nexport function toFilenameStem(label: string, fallback = 'suite'): string {\n  const stem = label\n    .trim()\n    .toLowerCase()\n    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '_')\n    .replace(/^_+|_+$/g, '');\n  return stem || fallback;\n}\n"
}

The new suite\n * is owned by the importing user, like create.\n */\nexport function ImportSuiteDrawer({\n  open,\n  connections,\n  onClose,\n  onImported,\n}: {\n  open: boolean;\n  /** Datasource connections the document can be imported onto. */\n  connections: Connection[];\n  onClose: () => void;\n  onImported: (suite: Suite) => void;\n}) {\n  const { message } = App.useApp();\n  const [connectionId, setConnectionId] = useState<string>();\n  const [doc, setDoc] = useState<SuiteDocument | null>(null);\n  const [fileName, setFileName] = useState<string>();\n  const [parseError, setParseError] = useState<string>();\n  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);\n\n  // Reset everything each time the drawer opens — a stale document/connection\n  // from a previous (possibly cancelled) import must not leak into the next one.\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!open) return;\n    setConnectionId(undefined);\n    setDoc(null);\n    setFileName(undefined);\n    setParseError(undefined);\n  }, [open]);\n\n  // Parse + shape-check the dropped file; return false so antd never uploads it.\n  const onFile = (file: File) => {\n    file\n      .text()\n      .then((text) => {\n        const parsed = parseSuiteDocument(text);\n        setDoc(parsed);\n        setFileName(file.name);\n        setParseError(undefined);\n      })\n      .catch((err: unknown) => {\n        setDoc(null);\n        setFileName(file.name);\n        setParseError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Could not read the file.');\n      });\n    return false;\n  };\n\n  const onSubmit = async () => {\n    if (!doc || !connectionId) return;\n    setSubmitting(true);\n    try {\n      const suite = await importSuite({ connection_id: connectionId, document: doc });\n      message.success(`${suite.name}: imported`);\n      onImported(suite);\n    } catch (err) {\n      message.error(`Import failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);\n    } finally {\n      setSubmitting(false);\n    }\n  };\n\n  const fileList: UploadFile[] = fileName\n    ? [{ uid: '1', name: fileName, status: parseError ? 'error' : 'done' }]\n    : [];\n\n  return (\n    <Drawer\n      title=\"Import suite\"\n      open={open}\n      onClose={onClose}\n      width={480}\n      destroyOnHidden\n      extra={\n        <Flex gap={8}>\n          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>\n          <Button\n            type=\"primary\"\n            loading={submitting}\n            disabled={!doc || !connectionId}\n            onClick={onSubmit}\n          >\n            Import\n          </Button>\n        </Flex>\n      }\n    >\n      <Flex vertical gap={16}>\n        <Upload.Dragger\n          accept=\"application/json,.json\"\n          multiple={false}\n          maxCount={1}\n          beforeUpload={onFile}\n          fileList={fileList}\n          onRemove={() => {\n            setDoc(null);\n            setFileName(undefined);\n            setParseError(undefined);\n          }}\n        >\n          <p className=\"ant-upload-drag-icon\">\n            <InboxOutlined />\n          </p>\n          <p className=\"ant-upload-text\">Click or drag a suite export (.json) here</p>\n          <p className=\"ant-upload-hint\">\n            A document produced by “Export” on any suite — checks, thresholds and config.\n          </p>\n        </Upload.Dragger>\n\n        {parseError && <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message=\"Invalid document\" description={parseError} />}\n\n        {doc && (\n          <Descriptions size=\"small\" column={1} bordered styles={{ label: { width: 120 } }}>\n            <Descriptions.Item label=\"Name\">{doc.name}</Descriptions.Item>\n            <Descriptions.Item label=\"Checks\">{doc.checks.length}</Descriptions.Item>\n            {doc.description && (\n              <Descriptions.Item label=\"Description\">{doc.description}</Descriptions.Item>\n            )}\n          </Descriptions>\n        )}\n\n        <Form layout=\"vertical\">\n          <Form.Item\n            label=\"Import onto connection\"\n            required\n            extra=\"The imported suite runs against this connection’s datasource.\"\n          >\n            <Select\n              value={connectionId}\n              onChange={setConnectionId}\n              placeholder=\"Select a connection\"\n              options={connections.map((c) => ({\n                value: c.id,\n                label: `${c.name} · ${CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[c.type]} · ${envLabel(c.env)}`,\n              }))}\n            />\n          </Form.Item>\n        </Form>\n\n        {connections.length === 0 && (\n          <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">\n            Create a datasource connection first — a suite must import onto one.\n          </Typography.Text>\n        )}\n      </Flex>\n    </Drawer>\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Parse the uploaded text as a suite export document, validating just enough of\n * the shape to fail fast on the wrong file (a random JSON, a half-document). The\n * object is otherwise passed through untouched so thresholds/config round-trip\n * exactly on import. Throws an `Error` with a user-facing message on any miss.\n */\nfunction parseSuiteDocument(text: string): SuiteDocument {\n  let parsed: unknown;\n  try {\n    parsed = JSON.parse(text);\n  } catch {\n    throw new Error('Not valid JSON.');\n  }\n  if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') {\n    throw new Error('Expected a suite document object.');\n  }\n  const obj = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;\n  if (typeof obj.name !== 'string' || !obj.name) {\n    throw new Error('Missing a suite “name” — is this a suite export?');\n  }\n  if (!Array.isArray(obj.checks)) {\n    throw new Error('Missing a “checks” list — is this a suite export?');\n  }\n  return parsed as SuiteDocument;\n}\n"
}

115:- [x] ✅ API: CRUD for suites and GX expectations (Snowflake path) — **suites** (PR-B1): `suite_service` + `/suites` CRUD (`connection_id` validated then immutable; delete cascades to checks). **checks** (PR-B2): `check_service` + nested `/suites/{id}/checks` CRUD surfacing `kind` + `warn/fail/critical_threshold` + GX `expectation_type`/`config`. v1 monitor-kind guard (only `expectation`; reserved kinds → 422, ADR 0012); checks scoped to their suite (cross-suite access → 404); thresholds are `Decimal` in (exact `Numeric` storage) / `float` out (clean JSON). 24 TestClient tests; all four modules 100%. Share-based access filtering deferred to the suite-sharing task; **DQ-dimension classification** deferred + tracked ([#124](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/124))
116:- [x] ✅ API: suite sharing — assign users with owner / editor / viewer roles — **sharing API + authz core** (PR-E1): `suite_authz.require_permission` (404-hides a suite with no access, 403s an insufficient level) + `share_service` + `/suites/{id}/shares` CRUD. Schema vocab `view`/`edit`/`admin` + implicit owner=`created_by`; **admin can delete + manage shares** (per decision); grant-to-owner/unknown → 422; manage needs `admin`, list needs `view`. **Enforcement** (PR-E2): `require_permission` applied across the suite endpoints (GET=view, PATCH=edit, DELETE=admin) + all check endpoints (reads=view, writes=edit); `list_suites` scoped to owned-or-shared. Lands the access control deferred in B1/B2. ~26 TestClient tests across the matrix acting as different users (viewer reads-not-writes, editor writes-not-deletes, admin deletes, outsider→404, list scoping); shares/suites/checks routes + share_service all 100%
117:- [x] ✅ API: suite export to JSON + import from JSON — `suite_io_service` + `GET /suites/{id}/export` (view) / `POST /suites/import` (any authed user, like create). Document is **connection-agnostic** — omits all DB identity (`id`/`connection_id`/`created_by`/timestamps), so it's a reusable template; import **re-binds** to a freshly chosen `connection_id` and owns the new suite as the importer. Round-trippable: thresholds are `Decimal` in/out (exact). Import is **atomic** — every check kind is validated before any row is written (bad doc → 422, nothing persisted); unknown `version` → 422; missing connection → 422. Checks emitted in stable creation order (diffable). Reuses `check_service.validate_kind` (no dup). 7 TestClient tests (no-identity-leak, view-gated, owned-by-importer, export→import→export round-trip, unknown-connection/version/kind-atomic); `suite_io_service` + `suites.py` 100%
