193:**Week 4 total: 18 / 26 ✅ (+2 🟡, 1 🔵)** _(connection manager UI complete (6/6); check editor core shipped + **dry-run preview** (PR-D1) + **column profiler panel** (PR-D2); **GX-Cloud redesign complete (4/4)** — classified connection + check create pages, edit-only drawers, suite-route/categorized picker (PR-A1/A2/B1/B2); PR-3c polish 2/3 (Settings `forbid` 🔵 blocked on the `.env` split) — sharing/admin UI + Monaco custom-SQL remain)_
204:- [x] ✅ **Check target table/path** — modeled as a **per-suite** datasource-shaped `Suite.target` (JSONB, shaped like the column-profiler request: `table`/`schema`/`catalog`/`path`/`file_format`), since `execute_run` runs all of a suite's checks against one batch (the GX data-asset-per-suite shape). `services/run_target.resolve_target` resolves it per connection type to the runner's `(table, schema, catalog)` triple (flat-file path rides the table-shaped `CheckRunner`'s `table` slot); `validate_target` is the write-time 422 guard on suite create/update. Migration `b1f2c3d4e5a6` (additive nullable column, tested up/down on Postgres). **Dispatch ungated**: `_trigger_suites` now hands each created run to `run_suite.delay` (lazy import — worker↔service cycle), broker-fail marks the run `failed`; `run_suite` resolves the target from the suite (targetless → clean `failed`), so the worker no longer takes a `table` arg; stale `until_week3` wording removed. 13 resolver units + worker/orchestration/suite-API target tests. _(Re-tracked from Week 3; [#215](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/215); PR-C0a)_
205:- [x] ✅ **Manual run trigger + run/result read API** — `POST /suites/{id}/run` queues a `Run` and dispatches it via the shared `run_dispatch.dispatch_run` helper (**edit**-gated — the capability ladder grants "trigger runs" at edit); the suite target (#215) is resolved **up front** so a targetless/misconfigured suite fails fast with 422 instead of a queued→failed run, and a broker outage marks the run `failed` + returns 503 (same contract as the probe). New `api/v1/runs.py` read surface for the results page: `GET /runs?suite_id=&status=&limit=` and `GET /runs/{id}` (run + joined `Result`s) are **suite-scoped** — the list filters to accessible suites and the detail gates on `require_permission(view)`, so per-suite sharing + existence-hiding hold (exactly why direct-Postgres/Grafana is rejected as the primary surface); `GET /pipeline_runs?provider=&status=` is the orchestration monitoring feed (auth-only, not suite-scoped). Read helpers live in `run_service.list_runs/get_run/list_results` + `orchestration_service.list_pipeline_runs`. 14 DB-backed API tests (trigger happy/targetless-422/edit-403/no-access-404/broker-503; list scoping+filters+limit; detail+results / 404s; pipeline filters + auth). _(Run-enablement gap; PR-C0b; gates the Week-6 Results page PR-C1)_
236:> **Build as an in-app React page** (the GX-Cloud-style redesign Phase C), **not Grafana** — reading Postgres directly would bypass DataQ's per-suite sharing + PII redaction; Grafana is deferred to an optional post-v1 ops add-on ([ADR 0018](adr/0018-results-surface-and-grafana-deferral.md), accepted). The Week-5 run-enablement backend it gates on is **done**: `runs.py` read endpoints (`GET /runs`, `GET /runs/{id}`, `GET /pipeline_runs`) + `POST /suites/{id}/run` (PR-C0b); [#215](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/215) target (PR-C0a). The `results.metric_value`/`duration_ms` columns were seam-built for these trend charts (ADR 0012).

+import { InboxOutlined } from '@ant-design/icons';
+import {

+import { CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS, type Connection, envLabel } from '../../api/connections';

+
+/**
+ * Import a portable suite document (the JSON produced by "Export") onto a chosen
+ * connection. The file is parsed + shape-checked client-side, then handed back to
+ * the backend unchanged (`POST /suites/import`) so thresholds/config round-trip
+ * exactly — the connection is the only thing the importer supplies. The new suite
+ * is owned by the importing user, like create.
+ */
+export function ImportSuiteDrawer({
+  open,
+  connections,
+  onClose,
+  onImported,
+}: {
+  open: boolean;
+  /** Datasource connections the document can be imported onto. */
+  connections: Connection[];
+  onClose: () => void;
+  onImported: (suite: Suite) => void;
+}) {
+  const { message } = App.useApp();
+  const [connectionId, setConnectionId] = useState<string>();
+  const [doc, setDoc] = useState<SuiteDocument | null>(null);
+  const [fileName, setFileName] = useState<string>();
+  const [parseError, setParseError] = useState<string>();
+  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
+
+  // Reset everything when the drawer (re)opens — a stale document/connection from
+  // a previous (possibly cancelled) import must not leak into the next one. The
+  // Drawer host stays mounted across open/close (it isn't destroyed), so this is
+  // a render-phase "adjust state when a prop changes" reset, matching the editor
+  // panels — not an effect.
+  const [prevOpen, setPrevOpen] = useState(open);
+  if (open !== prevOpen) {
+    setPrevOpen(open);
+    if (open) {
+      setConnectionId(undefined);
+      setDoc(null);
+      setFileName(undefined);
+      setParseError(undefined);
+    }
+  }
+
+  // Parse + shape-check the dropped file; return false so antd never uploads it.
+  const onFile = (file: File) => {
+    file
+      .text()
+      .then((text) => {
+        const parsed = parseSuiteDocument(text);
+        setDoc(parsed);
+        setFileName(file.name);
+        setParseError(undefined);
+      })
+      .catch((err: unknown) => {
+        setDoc(null);
+        setFileName(file.name);
+        setParseError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Could not read the file.');
+      });
+    return false;
+  };
+
+  const onSubmit = async () => {
+    if (!doc || !connectionId) return;
+    setSubmitting(true);
+    try {
+      const suite = await importSuite({ connection_id: connectionId, document: doc });
+      message.success(`${suite.name}: imported`);
+      onImported(suite);
+    } catch (err) {
+      message.error(`Import failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
+    } finally {
+      setSubmitting(false);
+    }
+  };
+
+  const fileList: UploadFile[] = fileName
+    ? [{ uid: '1', name: fileName, status: parseError ? 'error' : 'done' }]
+    : [];
+
+  return (
+    <Drawer
+      title="Import suite"
+      open={open}
+      onClose={onClose}
+      width={480}
+      destroyOnHidden
+      extra={
+        <Flex gap={8}>
+          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
+          <Button
+            type="primary"
+            loading={submitting}
+            disabled={!doc || !connectionId}
+            onClick={onSubmit}
+          >
+            Import
+          </Button>
+        </Flex>
+      }
+    >
+      <Flex vertical gap={16}>
+        <Upload.Dragger
+          accept="application/json,.json"
+          multiple={false}
+          maxCount={1}
+          beforeUpload={onFile}
+          fileList={fileList}
+          onRemove={() => {
+            setDoc(null);
+            setFileName(undefined);
+            setParseError(undefined);
+          }}
+        >
+          <p className="ant-upload-drag-icon">
+            <InboxOutlined />
+          </p>
+          <p className="ant-upload-text">Click or drag a suite export (.json) here</p>
+          <p className="ant-upload-hint">
+            A document produced by “Export” on any suite — checks, thresholds and config.
+          </p>
+        </Upload.Dragger>
+
+        {parseError && (
+          <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Invalid document" description={parseError} />
+        )}
+
+        {doc && (
+          <Descriptions size="small" column={1} bordered styles={{ label: { width: 120 } }}>
+            <Descriptions.Item label="Name">{doc.name}</Descriptions.Item>
+            <Descriptions.Item label="Checks">{doc.checks.length}</Descriptions.Item>
+            {doc.description && (
+              <Descriptions.Item label="Description">{doc.description}</Descriptions.Item>
+            )}
+          </Descriptions>
+        )}
+
+        <Form layout="vertical">
+          <Form.Item
+            label="Import onto connection"
+            required
+            extra="The imported suite runs against this connection’s datasource."
+          >
+            <Select
+              value={connectionId}
+              onChange={setConnectionId}
+              placeholder="Select a connection"
+              options={connections.map((c) => ({
+                value: c.id,
+                label: `${c.name} · ${CONNECTION_TYPE_LABELS[c.type]} · ${envLabel(c.env)}`,
+              }))}
+            />
+          </Form.Item>
+        </Form>
+
+        {connections.length === 0 && (
+          <Typography.Text type="secondary">
+            Create a datasource connection first — a suite must import onto one.
+          </Typography.Text>
+        )}
+      </Flex>
+    </Drawer>
+  );
+}
+
+/**
+ * Parse the uploaded text as a suite export document, validating just enough of
+ * the shape to fail fast on the wrong file (a random JSON, a half-document). The
+ * object is otherwise passed through untouched so thresholds/config round-trip
+ * exactly on import. Throws an `Error` with a user-facing message on any miss.
+ */
+function parseSuiteDocument(text: string): SuiteDocument {
+  let parsed: unknown;
+  try {
+    parsed = JSON.parse(text);
+  } catch {
+    throw new Error('Not valid JSON.');
+  }
+  if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object') {
+    throw new Error('Expected a suite document object.');
+  }
+  const obj = parsed as Record<string, unknown>;
+  if (typeof obj.name !== 'string' || !obj.name) {
+    throw new Error('Missing a suite “name” — is this a suite export?');
+  }
+  if (!Array.isArray(obj.checks)) {
+    throw new Error('Missing a “checks” list — is this a suite export?');
+  }
+  return parsed as SuiteDocument;
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+/**
+ * Trigger a browser download of `data` serialised as pretty-printed JSON.
+ *
+ * Builds an object-URL blob and clicks a transient anchor — the standard
+ * no-backend "save this JSON" path (used by the suite export). The URL is
+ * revoked immediately after the click so the blob doesn't leak.
+ */
+export function downloadJson(filename: string, data: unknown): void {
+  const blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' });
+  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
+  const anchor = document.createElement('a');
+  anchor.href = url;
+  anchor.download = filename;
+  document.body.appendChild(anchor);
+  anchor.click();
+  anchor.remove();
+  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Turn an arbitrary label into a safe, lowercase filename stem: non-word
+ * characters collapse to underscores, runs trim to one, leading/trailing
+ * underscores drop. Falls back to `fallback` when nothing usable remains (e.g.
+ * a name of only punctuation).
+ */
+export function toFilenameStem(label: string, fallback = 'suite'): string {
+  const stem = label
+    .trim()
+    .toLowerCase()
+    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '_')
+    .replace(/^_+|_+$/g, '');
+  return stem || fallback;
+}

75	> **Auth-boundary discipline (per [ADR 0010](adr/0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md)):** new connection-CRUD endpoints (and every protected route from here on) depend on a generic internal "current user" dependency that returns DataQ's own `User` — they must NOT read MSAL token claims directly in route/service code. Cheap now; expensive to retrofit once dozens of endpoints exist. No new abstraction layer required, just the boundary.

78	- [x] ✅ API: CRUD for Snowflake connections (DEV / QA / UAT), connection test endpoint — [PR 5](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/85) _(also introduced the `ConnectionAdapter` seam + registry per [ADR 0011](adr/0011-extensibility-seams-for-deferred-integrations.md), and `SecretStore.set` write-through — so PRs 6-8 are pure adapter additions)_
79	- [x] ✅ API: CRUD for ADF connections (subscription ID + service principal) — PR 6 _(`ADFConnectionAdapter` in the new `orchestration/` package — NOT `datasources/`, per CLAUDE.md §4; `test()` does SP token + factory GET via httpx. Enforces `(type, env)` uniqueness for orchestrator rows via a **partial unique index** `WHERE type IN ('adf','airflow')` per [#72](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/72) / ADR 0004 — datasources excluded, so Snowflake stays many-per-env. CRUD/API reused unchanged: pure adapter + registry + migration addition.)_
80	- [x] ✅ Connection re-auth endpoint — refresh expired Key Vault token — `POST /connections/{id}/reauth` (`svc.reauth_connection`): rotates the credential through `SecretStore.set` **and** verifies it via the same adapter probe as `/test`, in one step (the gap PATCH+`/test` leave open). Rotation persists before the probe, so a bad new credential surfaces as 502 `connection_test_failed`; a store-write failure is 502 `connection_secret_write_failed` with the old credential untouched. 6 TestClient tests (rotate+verify ok, failed-verify-but-rotation-persists, write-fail 502, 404, secret-required 422). Type-agnostic — applies to all six connection types
81	- [x] ✅ Review `connections.secret_ref` nullability — decide based on Airflow basic-poll / unauthenticated S3 cases ([PR #41 nit](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/41)) — **decision: keep nullable.** It's NULL for the transient flush→secret-write window (create), for credential-less auth (managed-identity/IAM-role, W7, ADR 0010/0011), and for unauthenticated sources. v1 types are all secret-bearing, but presence is enforced in the **service layer** (`test_connection` → 502 without a credential), not the schema — so W7 credential-less modes need no later migration. Recorded as a comment on the `secret_ref` column in `db/models.py`

133	### Column profiler (3 tasks — 3/3 ✅)
134	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Snowflake) — nulls, distinct count, min / max, top values — `profile_service` + `POST /suites/{id}/profile` (require_permission **edit**, suite-scoped so the connection is access-gated). Reads-only, persists nothing: one aggregate query (row count + null/distinct/min/max per column) + one top-N-values query per column, then `assemble_profile`. **SQL-injection-safe** — queries are built with the **SQLAlchemy Core expression language** (`select`/`table`/`column`, dialect-quoted) so there's no raw-string SQL sink (no S608/B608/CodeQL `py/sql-injection`); identifiers are additionally allowlist-validated (`validate_identifier`, strict `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$`) as defence-in-depth + a clean early 422, and `top_n` is `int()`-coerced. v1 → 422: non-Snowflake type (dispatch generalises Week 5), bad identifier, no schema; execution failure → 502 (adapter exception never echoed). min/max/top-values NaN-sanitised. 28 tests (22 pure: identifier allowlist incl. injection strings, compiled-SQL builders, assembly, div-by-zero, NaN; 6 endpoint via fake conn: stats, injection-422, unsupported-type-422, 502, edit-gated, no-schema-422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 90% (live `_open_connection` is the deferred warehouse seam)
135	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (ADLS / S3) — same stats via Pandas on sampled file — extended `profile_service` into a type dispatcher (`profile_connection`): SQL types → in-warehouse aggregation (unchanged), flat-file types (`adls_gen2`/`s3`) → download a **sample** of the file into Pandas and compute the same stats (`profile_dataframe`). Same `POST /suites/{id}/profile` endpoint, now polymorphic: SQL targets pass `table`/`schema`, flat-file targets pass `path` (+ optional `file_format`, else inferred from extension); response carries whichever identity applies. CSV + Parquet. **pandas "load less data" levers** (per the user's scale.html prompt): column projection (CSV `usecols`, Parquet `columns=` via pyarrow schema) so profiling 3 of N columns doesn't read all N, + row sampling (`_SAMPLE_ROWS`), + **zero-copy Arrow-backed dtypes** on the Parquet read (`dtype_backend="pyarrow"` — parquet is already Arrow, kept zero-copy; the stat helpers + `_to_native` are Arrow-scalar/`pd.NA`-safe). Stats are vectorised pandas (no Python row loops — enhancingperf N/A; CoW is a no-op for a read-only profiler + a process-global flag, so not toggled; pyarrow CSV engine rejected — it's incompatible with `nrows`/callable-`usecols`). NaN/Timestamp→JSON-safe. v1 → 422: unsupported type (UC still pending), missing target, unknown format, missing column; read failure → 502 (exception never echoed). Reuses `ColumnProfile`/`ProfileResult`. 24 new tests (pure `profile_dataframe`/`infer_file_format`/`_to_native`/projection-parse + endpoint via fake `_read_dataframe`); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 85% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). _Deferred: streaming/range reads (whole object still downloaded before sampling) + out-of-core (Dask) — future work if profiling cost bites._
136	- [x] ✅ Column profiler endpoint (Unity Catalog) — via Databricks SQL Warehouse — added `unity_catalog` to the profiler's **SQL** branch (reuses `profile_table` + the SQLAlchemy Core query builders + `assemble_profile` — no duplicate aggregation logic). `_open_connection` now dispatches the engine by type (`_engine_args`): Snowflake URL or a `REDACTED` URL via the installed `databricks` SQLAlchemy dialect. UC's **3-level namespace** (`catalog.schema.table`) is handled by building the table with a `quoted_name(f"{catalog}.{schema}", quote=False)` so the dialect emits three dotted parts rather than quoting the dotted string as one — verified by compiling the real builders against the Databricks dialect. Injection-safe: every part (catalog/schema/table/column) is allowlist-validated (no raw-string SQL, no CodeQL py/sql-injection surface). Endpoint gained `catalog` (request + response); the dispatcher requires it for UC (`422 profile_target_invalid` if absent). 12 new tests (catalog-aware builders compiled to SQL, `_engine_args` URL dispatch, UC endpoint stats via the same fake conn, missing-catalog 422, bad-catalog-identifier 422); `suites.py` 100%, `profile_service` 86% (only the live `_open_connection`/`_download_bytes` network seams uncovered — deferred smoke). **Completes the column profiler across all 4 datasources.**

139	- [x] ✅ Check types for flat files: schema validation, row count, null checks, ~~freshness by filename date~~ — `FlatFileCheckRunner` (`datasources/flatfile.py`): downloads the file (S3/ADLS) into a pandas DataFrame and runs the suite's GX expectations against GX's **pandas DataFrame asset**, so all GX expectation-kind checks (schema/row-count/null/value checks) run against flat files. Extracted the shared GX machinery — snake_case→GX-class translation, GX-result→`SuiteOutcome` mapping, and the suite/validation-definition `run_expectations` flow — into `datasources/gx_runner.py` (reused by the Snowflake runner and the future UC runner; no duplication). Flat-file IO (`download_bytes` + full-file `read_dataframe`) moved to `flatfile.py` behind primitives (raw config + resolved secret, not the ORM — matches `build_snowflake_runner`), and the column profiler now shares it. Because GX runs **in-process on the DataFrame**, the run path is fully unit-tested with a canned frame (real GX execution, not mocked) — only the network download is the deferred-smoke seam. 16 new tests; `gx_runner` 100%, `flatfile` 76% (only `download_bytes` uncovered). _Connection-type → runner dispatch (Snowflake vs flat-file) is the Week-5 `run_suite` wiring; **freshness-by-filename** is the reserved `freshness` monitor kind (deferred, ADR 0012), not a GX expectation._
140	- [x] ✅ Batch resolution — resolve batching regex to matched files, pick latest or specific batch — `resolve_batch` (`datasources/flatfile.py`): a batch `pattern` is a regex whose **first capture group is the batch key**; `latest` selects the greatest key (lexicographic — ISO dates sort chronologically), falling back to the storage modified-time when the pattern has no group; `specific` selects the file whose key equals a given `batch`. `BatchNotFoundError` on no match / unknown batch. The filter+select logic is pure and fully unit-tested (8 tests); object listing (`list_files` — S3 `list_objects_v2` paginated / ADLS `list_blobs`) is the live seam, and `resolve_batch_file` composes list+resolve. _Wiring a check's target to a resolved batch path is the Week-5 `run_suite` dispatch._

28	}: {
29	  suiteId: string;
30	  expectationType: string | undefined;
31	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
32	  form: FormInstance;
33	}) {
34	  const [state, setState] = useState<
35	    | { status: 'idle' }
36	    | { status: 'running' }
37	    | { status: 'ok'; result: CheckDryRunResult }
38	    | { status: 'error'; error: string }
39	  >({ status: 'idle' });
40	
41	  // Clear a previous preview when the expectation changes — in the edit drawer
42	  // the picker switches type in-place (DryRunPreview stays mounted), so without
43	  // this the old result would linger, misattributed to the new expectation.
44	  // Render-phase reset (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern)
45	  // rather than an effect, so the stale result never paints.
46	  const [prevExpectation, setPrevExpectation] = useState(expectationType);
47	  if (expectationType !== prevExpectation) {
48	    setPrevExpectation(expectationType);
49	    setState({ status: 'idle' });
50	  }
51	
52	  const table = typeof target?.table === 'string' ? target.table : undefined;
53	  const schema = typeof target?.schema === 'string' ? target.schema : null;
54	
55	  const disabledReason = !expectationType
56	    ? 'Pick an expectation to preview it.'
57	    : !table
58	      ? 'Set a table target on the suite to preview against live data.'
59	      : undefined;
60	
61	  const run = async () => {
62	    if (!expectationType || !table) return;
63	    setState({ status: 'running' });
64	    try {
65	      // Reuse the create/update payload shaping so the preview runs exactly the
66	      // config (and thresholds) the saved check would — name is irrelevant here.
67	      const payload = buildCheckPayload({
68	        ...form.getFieldsValue(true),
69	        expectation_type: expectationType,
70	      });
71	      const result = await dryRunCheck(suiteId, {
72	        expectation_type: expectationType,
73	        config: payload.config,
74	        warn_threshold: payload.warn_threshold,
75	        fail_threshold: payload.fail_threshold,
76	        critical_threshold: payload.critical_threshold,
77	        table,
78	        schema,
79	      });
80	      setState({ status: 'ok', result });
81	    } catch (err) {
82	      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });
83	    }
84	  };
85	
86	  return (
87	    <Flex vertical gap={8}>
88	      <Flex gap={12} align="center">
89	        <Button onClick={run} loading={state.status === 'running'} disabled={!!disabledReason}>
90	          Dry-run preview
91	        </Button>
92	        {disabledReason && <Typography.Text type="secondary">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>}
93	      </Flex>
94	      {state.status === 'ok' && <DryRunResultView result={state.result} />}
95	      {state.status === 'error' && (
96	        <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Dry-run failed" description={state.error} />
97	      )}
98	    </Flex>
99	  );
100	}
101	
102	function DryRunResultView({ result }: { result: CheckDryRunResult }) {
103	  return (
104	    <Descriptions
105	      size="small"
106	      bordered
107	      column={1}
108	      styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}
109	      items={[
110	        {
111	          key: 'status',
112	          label: 'Result',
113	          children: (
114	            <Tag color={RESULT_STATUS_COLORS[result.status as ResultStatus]}>{result.status}</Tag>
115	          ),
116	        },
117	        {
118	          key: 'metric',
119	          label: 'Metric',
120	          children: result.metric_value === null ? '—' : result.metric_value,
121	        },
122	        {
123	          key: 'observed',
124	          label: 'Observed',
125	          children: result.observed_value ? (
126	            <Typography.Text code>{JSON.stringify(result.observed_value)}</Typography.Text>
127	          ) : (
128	            '—'
129	          ),
130	        },
131	        {
132	          key: 'expected',
133	          label: 'Expected',
134	          children: result.expected_value ? (
135	            <Typography.Text code>{JSON.stringify(result.expected_value)}</Typography.Text>
136	          ) : (
137	            '—'
138	          ),
139	        },
140	      ]}
141	    />
142	  );

161	def trigger_suite_run(
162	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
163	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
164	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
165	) -> RunRead:
166	    """Queue a run of the suite and dispatch it to the worker.
167	
168	    `edit` gates this (the capability ladder grants 'trigger runs' at edit). The
169	    suite's target (#215) is resolved up front so a targetless/misconfigured
170	    suite fails fast with a 422 instead of a queued→failed run the caller has to
171	    poll to discover. A broker outage marks the run `failed` (never left stuck
172	    `queued`) and surfaces 503 — the same contract as the probe endpoint.
173	    """
174	    suite = require_permission(db, suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="edit")
175	    connection = db.get(Connection, suite.connection_id)
176	    assert connection is not None  # FK is RESTRICT; a suite always has its connection
177	    # Raises SuiteTargetInvalidError (422) for a targetless / wrong-datasource target.
178	    run_target.resolve_target(connection.type, suite.target)
179	
180	    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status="queued", triggered_by=f"manual:{current_user.id}")
181	    db.add(run)
182	    db.commit()
183	    db.refresh(run)
184	
185	    try:
186	        run_dispatch.dispatch_run(run.id)
187	    except Exception as exc:  # broker unreachable — don't leave the run stuck queued
188	        # Mark with the canonical terminal-failed shape — finished_at set,
189	        # started_at NULL (it never started) — matching the pipeline-trigger
190	        # dispatch-failure path (orchestration_service._trigger_suites) so
191	        # run-history / duration views stay consistent across trigger paths.
192	        run.status = "failed"
193	        run.finished_at = datetime.now(UTC)
194	        db.commit()
195	        raise HTTPException(
196	            status_code=status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
197	            detail="failed to dispatch run",
198	        ) from exc
199	    return RunRead.model_validate(run)

21	 * Dedicated full-page check authoring flow (GX-Cloud style): pick a category →

24	 */
25	export function CheckNew() {

28	  const { message } = App.useApp();

30	  const [expectationType, setExpectationType] = useState<string>();
31	  const [form] = Form.useForm();
32	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
33	  // The suite's run target (#215) drives the dry-run preview's table/schema.
34	  const { state: suiteState } = useAsyncData(() =>
35	    suiteId ? getSuite(suiteId) : Promise.reject(new Error('no suite')),
36	  );
37	  const target = suiteState.status === 'ok' ? suiteState.data.target : null;
38	
39	  const backToSuite = () => navigate(suiteId ? `/suites/${suiteId}` : '/suites');
40	  const spec = expectationType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[expectationType] : undefined;
41	
42	  // Start the config form clean each time an expectation is (re)picked — after
43	  // the <Form> mounts (it only renders in the config step), so the store is
44	  // connected and a re-pick can't leak the prior expectation's fields.
45	  useEffect(() => {
46	    if (expectationType) form.resetFields();
47	  }, [expectationType, form]);
48	
49	  const onFinish = async (values: Record<string, unknown>) => {
50	    if (!suiteId || !expectationType) return;
51	    setSubmitting(true);
52	    try {
53	      await createCheck(
54	        suiteId,
55	        buildCheckPayload({ ...values, expectation_type: expectationType }),
56	      );
57	      message.success(`${values.name as string}: created`);
58	      backToSuite();
59	    } catch (err) {
60	      message.error(`Create failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
61	    } finally {
62	      setSubmitting(false);
63	    }
64	  };
65	
66	  // Step 3 — config + thresholds for the chosen expectation.
67	  if (spec) {
68	    return (
69	      <Flex vertical gap={24} style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>

73	          backLabel="Back to expectations"

77	            {spec.description}
78	          </Typography.Paragraph>
79	          <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
80	            <Input placeholder="e.g. order_id not null" />
81	          </Form.Item>

91	                target={target}

93	              />
94	            </Form.Item>

10	/**
11	 * Edit a GX check. The expectation Select (grouped by category) drives which
12	 * config fields render (from the expectation catalog); the submitted `config` is
13	 * rebuilt from only the selected expectation's declared fields, so switching
14	 * types never leaks stale kwargs. Creating a check is the dedicated
15	 * `/suites/:suiteId/checks/new` page, not this drawer.
16	 */
17	export function CheckDrawer({
18	  open,
19	  suiteId,
20	  check,
21	  target,
22	  onClose,
23	  onSaved,
24	}: {
25	  open: boolean;
26	  suiteId: string;
27	  check?: Check;
28	  /** The suite's run target (#215) — drives the dry-run preview's table/schema. */
29	  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
30	  onClose: () => void;
31	  onSaved: () => void;
32	}) {
33	  const { message } = App.useApp();
34	  const [form] = Form.useForm();
35	  const [submitting, setSubmitting] = useState(false);
36	  const selectedType = Form.useWatch('expectation_type', form) as string | undefined;
37	  const spec = selectedType ? EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[selectedType] : undefined;
38	
39	  // Reset first (antd keeps values for unmounted fields, so stale config can
40	  // survive an open→close→open with a different check), then prefill.
41	  useEffect(() => {
42	    if (!open || !check) return;
43	    form.resetFields();
44	    form.setFieldsValue({
45	      name: check.name,
46	      expectation_type: check.expectation_type,
47	      config: configToForm(EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[check.expectation_type], check.config),
48	      warn_threshold: check.warn_threshold ?? undefined,
49	      fail_threshold: check.fail_threshold ?? undefined,
50	      critical_threshold: check.critical_threshold ?? undefined,
51	    });
52	  }, [open, check, form]);
53	
54	  const onSubmit = async () => {
55	    if (!check) return;
56	    let values: Record<string, unknown>;
57	    try {
58	      values = await form.validateFields();
59	    } catch {
60	      return; // inline validation errors
61	    }
62	    const payload = buildCheckPayload(values);
63	    setSubmitting(true);
64	    try {
65	      await updateCheck(suiteId, check.id, payload);
66	      message.success(`${payload.name}: saved`);
67	      onSaved();
68	    } catch (err) {
69	      message.error(`Save failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error'}`);
70	    } finally {
71	      setSubmitting(false);
72	    }
73	  };
74	
75	  return (
76	    <Drawer
77	      title={check ? `Edit “${check.name}”` : 'Edit check'}
78	      open={open}
79	      onClose={onClose}
80	      width={520}
81	      destroyOnHidden
82	      extra={
83	        <Flex gap={8}>
84	          <Button onClick={onClose}>Cancel</Button>
85	          <Button type="primary" loading={submitting} onClick={onSubmit}>
86	            Save
87	          </Button>
88	        </Flex>
89	      }
90	    >
91	      <Form form={form} layout="vertical">
92	        <Form.Item name="name" label="Name" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
93	          <Input placeholder="e.g. order_id not null" />
94	        </Form.Item>
95	        <Form.Item name="expectation_type" label="Expectation" rules={[{ required: true }]}>
96	          <Select

100	              label: g.category,
101	              options: g.specs.map((e) => ({ value: e.type, label: e.label })),
102	            }))}

114	          </>

121	          expectationType={selectedType}
122	          target={target}

124	        />

1	import type { CheckCreate } from '../../api/suites';
2	import { EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE, type ExpectationSpec } from './expectationCatalog';
3	
4	/**
5	 * Pure check-authoring form helpers shared by the edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`)
6	 * and the dedicated create page (`CheckNew`): the form↔payload conversions, so
7	 * the two surfaces can't drift on kwarg shaping. The matching field components
8	 * live in `checkFormFields.tsx`.
9	 */
10	
11	/** Split a comma-separated list field into trimmed, non-empty items. */
12	export function parseList(value: unknown): string[] {
13	  return String(value ?? '')
14	    .split(',')
15	    .map((s) => s.trim())
16	    .filter(Boolean);
17	}
18	
19	function numOrNull(v: unknown): number | null {
20	  return typeof v === 'number' ? v : null;
21	}
22	
23	/** Build the GX `config` kwargs from only the selected expectation's fields. */
24	function formToConfig(
25	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
26	  raw: Record<string, unknown>,
27	): Record<string, unknown> {
28	  const config: Record<string, unknown> = {};
29	  if (!spec) return config;
30	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
31	    const value = raw[field.name];
32	    if (value === undefined || value === null || value === '') continue;
33	    if (field.type === 'list') {
34	      const items = parseList(value);
35	      if (items.length > 0) config[field.name] = items;
36	    } else {
37	      config[field.name] = value;
38	    }
39	  }
40	  return config;
41	}
42	
43	/** Inverse of formToConfig for edit-mode prefill (list array → comma string). */
44	export function configToForm(
45	  spec: ExpectationSpec | undefined,
46	  config: Record<string, unknown>,
47	): Record<string, unknown> {
48	  const form: Record<string, unknown> = {};
49	  if (!spec) return form;
50	  for (const field of spec.fields) {
51	    const value = config[field.name];
52	    if (value === undefined) continue;
53	    form[field.name] = field.type === 'list' && Array.isArray(value) ? value.join(', ') : value;
54	  }
55	  return form;
56	}
57	
58	/** Assemble the create/update payload from validated form values. Rebuilds
59	 *  `config` from only the selected expectation's fields, so switching types
60	 *  never leaks stale kwargs. */
61	export function buildCheckPayload(values: Record<string, unknown>): CheckCreate {
62	  const spec = EXPECTATION_BY_TYPE[values.expectation_type as string];
63	  return {
64	    name: values.name as string,
65	    expectation_type: values.expectation_type as string,
66	    config: formToConfig(spec, (values.config ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>),
67	    warn_threshold: numOrNull(values.warn_threshold),
68	    fail_threshold: numOrNull(values.fail_threshold),
69	    critical_threshold: numOrNull(values.critical_threshold),
70	  };
71	}

1	import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react';
2	
3	/** Three-state result of an async fetch. */
4	export type AsyncState<T> =
5	  | { status: 'loading' }
6	  | { status: 'ok'; data: T }
7	  | { status: 'error'; error: string };
8	
9	/**
10	 * Fetch on mount (and on `reload()`), with a cancelled-guard so a late
11	 * resolution after unmount doesn't set state, and rejection normalised to a
12	 * string `error`. Shared by the data pages (Home, Connections, …) so the
13	 * cancelled-effect dance lives in one place rather than being re-derived per page.
14	 *
15	 * `reload` re-runs the fetcher (e.g. after a mutation) while keeping the current
16	 * data visible until the refetch resolves — no flash back to the loading state.
17	 */
18	export function useAsyncData<T>(fetcher: () => Promise<T>): {
19	  state: AsyncState<T>;
20	  reload: () => void;
21	} {
22	  const [state, setState] = useState<AsyncState<T>>({ status: 'loading' });
23	  const [nonce, setNonce] = useState(0);
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    let cancelled = false;
27	    fetcher()
28	      .then((data) => {
29	        if (!cancelled) setState({ status: 'ok', data });
30	      })
31	      .catch((err: unknown) => {
32	        if (!cancelled) {
33	          setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
34	        }
35	      });
36	    return () => {
37	      cancelled = true;
38	    };
39	    // Re-run on mount and whenever `reload` bumps the nonce; the fetcher identity
40	    // is intentionally not a dependency.
41	    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
42	  }, [nonce]);
43	
44	  const reload = useCallback(() => setNonce((n) => n + 1), []);
45	  return { state, reload };
46	}
47	
```

  "new_string": "export async function dryRunCheck(\n  suiteId: string,\n  payload: CheckDryRunRequest,\n): Promise<CheckDryRunResult> {\n  const { data } = await api.post<CheckDryRunResult>(`/suites/${suiteId}/checks/dryrun`, payload);\n  return data;\n}\n\n/** Mirrors the backend `ColumnProfileRequest` — profile columns of the suite's\n *  table/file (no persistence). The target identity (`table`/`schema`/`catalog`\n *  for SQL, `path`/`file_format` for flat files) comes from the suite's run\n *  target (#215); `columns` is the subset to profile. */\nexport interface ColumnProfileRequest {\n  columns: string[];\n  top_n?: number;\n  table?: string | null;\n  schema?: string | null;\n  catalog?: string | null;\n  path?: string | null;\n  file_format?: 'csv' | 'parquet' | null;\n}\n\n/** Mirrors the backend `TopValue` — a value and how often it occurs. */\nexport interface TopValue {\n  value: unknown;\n  count: number;\n}\n\n/** Mirrors the backend `ColumnProfileRead` — per-column stats. */\nexport interface ColumnProfile {\n  column: string;\n  null_count: number;\n  null_fraction: number;\n  distinct_count: number | null;\n  min_value: unknown;\n  max_value: unknown;\n  top_values: TopValue[];\n}\n\n/** Mirrors the backend `ProfileRead` — row count + per-column stats. Identity\n *  fields are type-specific (SQL fills `table`/`schema`/`catalog`, flat files\n *  fill `path`/`file_format`). */\nexport interface ProfileResult {\n  row_count: number;\n  columns: ColumnProfile[];\n  table?: string | null;\n  schema?: string | null;\n  catalog?: string | null;\n  path?: string | null;\n  file_format?: string | null;\n}\n\nexport async function profileColumns(\n  suiteId: string,\n  payload: ColumnProfileRequest,\n): Promise<ProfileResult> {\n  const { data } = await api.post<ProfileResult>(`/suites/${suiteId}/profile`, payload);\n  return data;\n}"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/frontend/src/components/checks/ColumnProfilePanel.tsx",
  "content": "import { Alert, Button, Collapse, Descriptions, Flex, Input, Table, Typography } from 'antd';\nimport { useState } from 'react';\n\nimport { type ColumnProfile, profileColumns, type ProfileResult } from '../../api/suites';\n\n/**\n * Inline column-profiler panel for the check editor: profiles one column of the\n * suite's run target (#215) — nulls, distinct count, min/max, top values — so\n * the author can ground a check's config (a value range, an allowed set, a null\n * threshold) in the real data before saving. Reads-only, persists nothing\n * (`POST /suites/{id}/profile`). Shared by the create page (`CheckNew`) and the\n * edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`).\n *\n * The profiled column pre-fills from the check's `column` config field (so\n * picking a column for the expectation primes the profiler), but stays editable\n * so the author can explore neighbouring columns. Collapsed by default to keep\n * the editor uncluttered — it's an opt-in aid, not always-on.\n *\n * Backend limits surface as the API's error message (e.g. no credential,\n * unreachable warehouse); the button is disabled with a reason until the suite\n * has a table/file target and a column is entered.\n */\nexport function ColumnProfilePanel({\n  suiteId,\n  target,\n  column,\n}: {\n  suiteId: string;\n  /** The suite's run target (#215) — supplies the table/file identity. */\n  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;\n  /** The check's currently-selected column, used to pre-fill the input. */\n  column: string | undefined;\n}) {\n  const profileTarget = extractProfileTarget(target);\n\n  // Pre-fill from the check's column, but let the author override. Render-phase\n  // sync (React's \"adjust state when a prop changes\" pattern) so picking the\n  // expectation's column primes the input without an effect round-trip.\n  const [value, setValue] = useState(column ?? '');\n  const [prevColumn, setPrevColumn] = useState(column);\n  if (column !== prevColumn) {\n    setPrevColumn(column);\n    if (column) setValue(column);\n  }\n\n  const [state, setState] = useState<\n    | { status: 'idle' }\n    | { status: 'running' }\n    | { status: 'ok'; result: ProfileResult }\n    | { status: 'error'; error: string }\n  >({ status: 'idle' });\n\n  const disabledReason = !profileTarget\n    ? 'Set a table or file target on the suite to profile.'\n    : !value.trim()\n      ? 'Enter a column to profile.'\n      : undefined;\n\n  const run = async () => {\n    if (!profileTarget || !value.trim()) return;\n    setState({ status: 'running' });\n    try {\n      const result = await profileColumns(suiteId, {\n        columns: [value.trim()],\n        ...profileTarget,\n      });\n      setState({ status: 'ok', result });\n    } catch (err) {\n      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });\n    }\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Collapse\n      size=\"small\"\n      items={[\n        {\n          key: 'profiler',\n          label: 'Column profiler',\n          children: (\n            <Flex vertical gap={8}>\n              <Flex gap={8} align=\"center\" wrap>\n                <Input\n                  value={value}\n                  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}\n                  placeholder=\"Column to profile\"\n                  style={{ maxWidth: 240 }}\n                  onPressEnter={run}\n                />\n                <Button\n                  onClick={run}\n                  loading={state.status === 'running'}\n                  disabled={!!disabledReason}\n                >\n                  Profile\n                </Button>\n                {disabledReason && (\n                  <Typography.Text type=\"secondary\">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>\n                )}\n              </Flex>\n              {state.status === 'ok' && <ProfileView result={state.result} />}\n              {state.status === 'error' && (\n                <Alert type=\"error\" showIcon message=\"Profile failed\" description={state.error} />\n              )}\n            </Flex>\n          ),\n        },\n      ]}\n    />\n  );\n}\n\n/** Pull the datasource-shaped identity out of the suite target, or null when no\n *  profilable target is set (the backend needs a `table` or a `path`). */\nfunction extractProfileTarget(\n  target: Record<string, unknown> | null,\n): Pick<\n  import('../../api/suites').ColumnProfileRequest,\n  'table' | 'schema' | 'catalog' | 'path' | 'file_format'\n> | null {\n  if (!target) return null;\n  const str = (k: string): string | undefined =>\n    typeof target[k] === 'string' ? (target[k] as string) : undefined;\n  const table = str('table');\n  const path = str('path');\n  if (!table && !path) return null;\n  return {\n    table,\n    schema: str('schema'),\n    catalog: str('catalog'),\n    path,\n    file_format: str('file_format') as 'csv' | 'parquet' | undefined,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction renderScalar(v: unknown): string {\n  if (v === null || v === undefined) return '—';\n  return typeof v === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(v) : String(v);\n}\n\nfunction ProfileView({ result }: { result: ProfileResult }) {\n  const col: ColumnProfile | undefined = result.columns[0];\n  if (!col) return null;\n  const nullPct = (col.null_fraction * 100).toFixed(1);\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical gap={8}>\n      <Descriptions\n        size=\"small\"\n        bordered\n        column={1}\n        styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}\n        items={[\n          { key: 'column', label: 'Column', children: col.column },\n          { key: 'rows', label: 'Row count', children: result.row_count },\n          {\n            key: 'nulls',\n            label: 'Nulls',\n            children: `${col.null_count} (${nullPct}%)`,\n          },\n          {\n            key: 'distinct',\n            label: 'Distinct',\n            children: col.distinct_count === null ? '—' : col.distinct_count,\n          },\n          { key: 'min', label: 'Min', children: renderScalar(col.min_value) },\n          { key: 'max', label: 'Max', children: renderScalar(col.max_value) },\n        ]}\n      />\n      {col.top_values.length > 0 && (\n        <Table\n          size=\"small\"\n          pagination={false}\n          rowKey={(_, i) => String(i)}\n          dataSource={col.top_values}\n          columns={[\n            { title: 'Top value', dataIndex: 'value', render: (v: unknown) => renderScalar(v) },\n            { title: 'Count', dataIndex: 'count', width: 100 },\n          ]}\n        />\n      )}\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}\n"
}

+/** Mirrors the backend `ColumnProfileRequest` — profile columns of the suite's
+ *  table/file (no persistence). The target identity (`table`/`schema`/`catalog`
+ *  for SQL, `path`/`file_format` for flat files) comes from the suite's run

+export interface ColumnProfileRequest {
+  columns: string[];
+  top_n?: number;
+  table?: string | null;
+  schema?: string | null;
+  catalog?: string | null;
+  path?: string | null;

+export interface ColumnProfile {
+  column: string;

+  null_fraction: number;
+  distinct_count: number | null;
+  min_value: unknown;
+  max_value: unknown;

+export interface ProfileResult {
+  row_count: number;
+  columns: ColumnProfile[];
+  table?: string | null;
+  schema?: string | null;
+  catalog?: string | null;
+  path?: string | null;
+  file_format?: string | null;
+}
+
+export async function profileColumns(
+  suiteId: string,
+  payload: ColumnProfileRequest,

+  profileColumns,
+  type ProfileResult,
+} from '../../api/suites';
+
+/**
+ * Inline column-profiler panel for the check editor: profiles one column of the
+ * suite's run target (#215) — nulls, distinct count, min/max, top values — so
+ * the author can ground a check's config (a value range, an allowed set, a null
+ * threshold) in the real data before saving. Reads-only, persists nothing
+ * (`POST /suites/{id}/profile`). Shared by the create page (`CheckNew`) and the
+ * edit drawer (`CheckDrawer`).
+ *
+ * The profiled column pre-fills from the check's `column` config field (so
+ * picking a column for the expectation primes the profiler), but stays editable
+ * so the author can explore neighbouring columns. Collapsed by default to keep
+ * the editor uncluttered — it's an opt-in aid, not always-on.
+ *
+ * Backend limits surface as the API's error message (e.g. no credential,
+ * unreachable warehouse); the button is disabled with a reason until the suite
+ * has a table/file target and a column is entered.
+ */
+export function ColumnProfilePanel({
+  suiteId,
+  target,
+  column,
+}: {
+  suiteId: string;
+  /** The suite's run target (#215) — supplies the table/file identity. */
+  target: Record<string, unknown> | null;
+  /** The check's currently-selected column, used to pre-fill the input. */
+  column: string | undefined;
+}) {
+  const profileTarget = extractProfileTarget(target);
+
+  // Pre-fill from the check's column, but let the author override. Render-phase
+  // sync (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern) so picking the
+  // expectation's column primes the input without an effect round-trip.
+  const [value, setValue] = useState(column ?? '');
+  const [prevColumn, setPrevColumn] = useState(column);
+  if (column !== prevColumn) {
+    setPrevColumn(column);
+    if (column) setValue(column);
+  }
+
+  const [state, setState] = useState<
+    | { status: 'idle' }
+    | { status: 'running' }
+    | { status: 'ok'; result: ProfileResult }
+    | { status: 'error'; error: string }
+  >({ status: 'idle' });
+
+  const disabledReason = !profileTarget
+    ? 'Set a table or file target on the suite to profile.'
+    : !value.trim()
+      ? 'Enter a column to profile.'
+      : undefined;
+
+  const run = async () => {
+    if (!profileTarget || !value.trim()) return;
+    setState({ status: 'running' });
+    try {
+      const result = await profileColumns(suiteId, {
+        columns: [value.trim()],
+        ...profileTarget,
+      });
+      setState({ status: 'ok', result });
+    } catch (err) {
+      setState({ status: 'error', error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'unknown error' });
+    }
+  };
+
+  return (
+    <Collapse
+      size="small"
+      items={[
+        {
+          key: 'profiler',
+          label: 'Column profiler',
+          children: (
+            <Flex vertical gap={8}>
+              <Flex gap={8} align="center" wrap>
+                <Input
+                  value={value}
+                  onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
+                  placeholder="Column to profile"
+                  style={{ maxWidth: 240 }}
+                  onPressEnter={run}
+                />
+                <Button
+                  onClick={run}
+                  loading={state.status === 'running'}
+                  disabled={!!disabledReason}
+                >
+                  Profile
+                </Button>
+                {disabledReason && (
+                  <Typography.Text type="secondary">{disabledReason}</Typography.Text>
+                )}
+              </Flex>
+              {state.status === 'ok' && <ProfileView result={state.result} />}
+              {state.status === 'error' && (
+                <Alert type="error" showIcon message="Profile failed" description={state.error} />
+              )}
+            </Flex>
+          ),
+        },
+      ]}
+    />
+  );
+}
+
+/** Pull the datasource-shaped identity out of the suite target, or null when no
+ *  profilable target is set (the backend needs a `table` or a `path`). */
+function extractProfileTarget(
+  target: Record<string, unknown> | null,
+): Pick<ColumnProfileRequest, 'table' | 'schema' | 'catalog' | 'path' | 'file_format'> | null {
+  if (!target) return null;
+  const str = (k: string): string | undefined =>
+    typeof target[k] === 'string' ? (target[k] as string) : undefined;
+  const table = str('table');
+  const path = str('path');
+  if (!table && !path) return null;
+  return {
+    table,
+    schema: str('schema'),
+    catalog: str('catalog'),
+    path,
+    file_format: str('file_format') as 'csv' | 'parquet' | undefined,
+  };
+}
+
+function renderScalar(v: unknown): string {
+  if (v === null || v === undefined) return '—';
+  return typeof v === 'object' ? JSON.stringify(v) : String(v);
+}
+
+function ProfileView({ result }: { result: ProfileResult }) {
+  const col: ColumnProfile | undefined = result.columns[0];
+  if (!col) return null;
+  const nullPct = (col.null_fraction * 100).toFixed(1);
+  return (
+    <Flex vertical gap={8}>
+      <Descriptions
+        size="small"
+        bordered
+        column={1}
+        styles={{ label: { width: 140 } }}
+        items={[
+          { key: 'column', label: 'Column', children: col.column },
+          { key: 'rows', label: 'Row count', children: result.row_count },
+          {
+            key: 'nulls',
+            label: 'Nulls',
+            children: `${col.null_count} (${nullPct}%)`,
+          },
+          {
+            key: 'distinct',
+            label: 'Distinct',
+            children: col.distinct_count === null ? '—' : col.distinct_count,
+          },
+          { key: 'min', label: 'Min', children: renderScalar(col.min_value) },
+          { key: 'max', label: 'Max', children: renderScalar(col.max_value) },
+        ]}
+      />
+      {col.top_values.length > 0 && (
+        <Table
+          size="small"
+          pagination={false}
+          rowKey={(_, i) => String(i)}
+          dataSource={col.top_values}
+          columns={[
+            { title: 'Top value', dataIndex: 'value', render: (v: unknown) => renderScalar(v) },
+            { title: 'Count', dataIndex: 'count', width: 100 },
+          ]}
+        />
+      )}
+    </Flex>
+  );
+}

The `column` config field name matches the watch path. The pre-fill works for column-scoped expectations.

I've thoroughly reviewed all three angles. The contract between the panel and backend holds: the frontend sends key `schema` (the alias), and Pydantic v2 accepts input by alias by default even without `populate_by_name` — so that is NOT a bug. The `CheckNew` fragment wrapping preserves prior behavior. No null-deref, falsy-zero, missing-await, or swallowed-error bugs found in the component logic.

No confirmed or plausible correctness bugs found.

Notes on the specific concerns raised:

- **`schema` field alias / `populate_by_name`**: Not a bug. The frontend sends the JSON key `schema` (both `extractProfileTarget` and the `ColumnProfileRequest` TS interface use `schema`). The backend field is `schema_ = Field(alias="schema")` without `populate_by_name=True`, but in Pydantic v2 the alias is the input key by default — so `schema` is exactly what's accepted. (Sending `schema_` would have failed; the panel correctly sends `schema`.) The suite `target` JSONB is also stored under `schema` via `SuiteTarget.to_storage()`'s `by_alias=True`, so `extractProfileTarget`'s `target['schema']` read lines up.

- **Request body shape**: Accepted. Body is `{ columns: [trimmed], table?, schema?, catalog?, path?, file_format? }`. `top_n` is omitted but has a backend default (`10`), and absent identity fields are `undefined` (dropped from JSON), satisfying the optional/nullable backend fields. `columns` has exactly one trimmed entry, meeting `min_length=1`.

- **CheckNew fragment change**: Behavior-preserving. The single `<Form.Item><DryRunPreview/></Form.Item>` was replaced by a fragment holding two sibling `Form.Item`s (profiler + dry-run), still gated by `suiteId &&`. No invariant dropped.

- **Render-phase column sync**: Correct. When `column` becomes `undefined` (field cleared), `prevColumn` updates but `value` is intentionally retained (`if (column) setValue(column)`), matching the documented "editable, pre-fill only on a real column" intent — not a falsy bug.

- **Error handling / await**: `run` awaits `profileColumns` and catches, surfacing `err.message`; no swallowed errors. The `!value.trim()` / `!profileTarget` guards and `disabledReason` use truthy string checks (no numeric-zero hazard since these are strings).

53	 * `1m 3s`. Returns an em dash when either bound is missing (queued / never
54	 * finished) or the interval is negative (clock skew).
55	 */
56	export function formatDuration(startedAt: string | null, finishedAt: string | null): string {
57	  if (!startedAt || !finishedAt) return '—';
58	  const ms = new Date(finishedAt).getTime() - new Date(startedAt).getTime();
59	  if (Number.isNaN(ms) || ms < 0) return '—';
60	  if (ms < 1000) return `${ms}ms`;
61	  const totalSeconds = Math.round(ms / 1000);
62	  if (totalSeconds < 60) return `${totalSeconds}s`;
63	  const minutes = Math.floor(totalSeconds / 60);

Done. Picked up and shipped the next Week-4 item: the **inline column-profiler panel** in the check editor.

## What landed — PR [#232](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/232)

`ColumnProfilePanel` — a collapsed-by-default panel shared by the create page ([CheckNew.tsx](frontend/src/pages/CheckNew.tsx)) and the edit drawer ([CheckDrawer.tsx](frontend/src/components/checks/CheckDrawer.tsx)). It profiles one column of the suite's run target (#215) via the existing `POST /suites/{id}/profile` (no persistence) and renders null count/fraction, distinct count, min/max, and top values — so an author can ground a range / allowed-set / null threshold in real data before saving.

Key behaviours:
- Column **pre-fills from the check's `column` config field** (render-phase prop-sync, same idiom as `DryRunPreview`) but stays editable.
- Target identity (`table`/`schema`/`catalog` for SQL, `path`/`file_format` for flat files) is pulled from the suite target.
- Disabled-with-reason until target + column present; backend limits surface as a clean error alert.
- Extracted `formatScalar` into the shared [resultsFormat.ts](frontend/src/components/results/resultsFormat.ts) and consumed it (renders falsy scalars `0`/`false`/`''` correctly, not as the em dash).

## Process
- **Review:** dispatched two review agents (correctness + cleanup) rather than self-review. Correctness found nothing (the `schema`-alias contract checks out). Cleanup found two reuse items — I applied the `formatScalar` extraction here and filed the broader migration (DryRunPreview/Results + a shared target extractor) as **[#231](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/231)** so nothing's silently dropped.
- **Verified locally:** 72 tests green, `tsc`/`eslint`/`prettier`/`vite build` all clean.
- **Docs:** updated [docs/progress.md](docs/progress.md) (Check editor UI 5/9, Week 4 18/26) and CLAUDE.md §13 headline.

Live warehouse/file profiling stays the deferred smoke (no DEV creds), consistent with the rest of the run path. CI is running on the PR now.

40	class ShareTargetInvalidError(DataQError):
41	    status_code = 422
42	    code = "share_target_invalid"
43	
44	
45	def _get_share(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> Share:
46	    share = session.scalars(
47	        select(Share).where(Share.suite_id == suite_id, Share.user_id == user_id)
48	    ).first()
49	    if share is None:
50	        raise ShareNotFoundError(
51	            "no share for this user on this suite",
52	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(user_id)},
53	        )
54	    return share
55	
56	
57	def grant_share(
58	    session: Session,
59	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
60	    *,
61	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
62	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
63	    permission: str,
64	) -> Share:
65	    """Grant `target_user_id` a permission on the suite. Actor needs `admin`."""
66	    suite = require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
67	    if target_user_id == suite.created_by:
68	        raise ShareTargetInvalidError(
69	            "cannot share a suite with its owner (already has full access)",
70	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(target_user_id)},
71	        )
72	    if session.get(User, target_user_id) is None:
73	        raise ShareTargetInvalidError(
74	            "target user does not exist", detail={"user_id": str(target_user_id)}
75	        )
76	
77	    share = Share(suite_id=suite_id, user_id=target_user_id, permission=permission)
78	    session.add(share)
79	    try:
80	        session.commit()
81	    except IntegrityError as exc:
82	        session.rollback()
83	        raise ShareConflictError(
84	            "user already has a share on this suite; use PATCH to change it",
85	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(target_user_id)},
86	        ) from exc
87	    session.refresh(share)
88	    log.info(
89	        "share_granted", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id), permission=permission
90	    )
91	    return share
92	
93	
94	def list_shares(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, *, actor_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[Share]:
95	    """List a suite's shares. Actor needs `view` (collaborators can see who else has access)."""
96	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="view")
97	    return list(
98	        session.scalars(select(Share).where(Share.suite_id == suite_id).order_by(Share.created_at))
99	    )
100	
101	
102	def update_share(
103	    session: Session,
104	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
105	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
106	    *,
107	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
108	    permission: str,
109	) -> Share:
110	    """Change a user's permission. Actor needs `admin`."""
111	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
112	    share = _get_share(session, suite_id, target_user_id)
113	    share.permission = permission
114	    session.commit()
115	    session.refresh(share)
116	    log.info(
117	        "share_updated", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id), permission=permission
118	    )
119	    return share
120	
121	
122	def revoke_share(
123	    session: Session,
124	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
125	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
126	    *,
127	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
128	) -> None:
129	    """Revoke a user's share. Actor needs `admin`."""
130	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
131	    share = _get_share(session, suite_id, target_user_id)
132	    session.delete(share)
133	    session.commit()
134	    log.info("share_revoked", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id))
135

1	"""Suite share endpoints — manage who can access a suite and at what level.
2	
3	Nested under the suite. Managing shares requires `admin` on the suite (owner
4	qualifies); listing requires `view`. Authorization + the 404-hide / 403 split
5	live in `suite_authz`; this layer just wires the current user as the actor.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import uuid
11	from typing import Annotated, Literal
12	
13	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status
14	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
15	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
16	
17	from backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user
18	from backend.app.db.models import User
19	from backend.app.db.session import get_db
20	from backend.app.services import share_service as svc
21	
22	router = APIRouter(tags=["shares"])
23	
24	# Grantable share levels — NOT 'owner' (that's the immutable creator, not a share).
25	SharePermission = Literal["view", "edit", "admin"]
26	
27	
28	class ShareCreate(BaseModel):
29	    user_id: uuid.UUID
30	    permission: SharePermission
31	
32	
33	class ShareUpdate(BaseModel):
34	    permission: SharePermission
35	
36	
37	class ShareRead(BaseModel):
38	    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
39	
40	    suite_id: uuid.UUID
41	    user_id: uuid.UUID
42	    permission: str
43	
44	
45	@router.post(
46	    "/suites/{suite_id}/shares",
47	    response_model=ShareRead,
48	    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
49	    summary="Share a suite with a user",
50	)
51	def grant_share(
52	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
53	    payload: ShareCreate,
54	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
55	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
56	) -> ShareRead:
57	    share = svc.grant_share(
58	        db,
59	        suite_id,
60	        actor_id=current_user.id,
61	        target_user_id=payload.user_id,
62	        permission=payload.permission,
63	    )
64	    return ShareRead.model_validate(share)
65	
66	
67	@router.get(
68	    "/suites/{suite_id}/shares",
69	    response_model=list[ShareRead],
70	    summary="List a suite's shares",
71	)
72	def list_shares(
73	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
74	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
75	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
76	) -> list[ShareRead]:
77	    return [
78	        ShareRead.model_validate(s) for s in svc.list_shares(db, suite_id, actor_id=current_user.id)
79	    ]
80	
81	
82	@router.patch(
83	    "/suites/{suite_id}/shares/{user_id}",
84	    response_model=ShareRead,
85	    summary="Change a user's permission on a suite",
86	)
87	def update_share(
88	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
89	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
90	    payload: ShareUpdate,
91	    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
92	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
93	) -> ShareRead:
94	    share = svc.update_share(
95	        db, suite_id, user_id, actor_id=current_user.id, permission=payload.permission
96	    )
97	    return ShareRead.model_validate(share)

102	    status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
103	    summary="Revoke a user's share",
104	)

109	    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
110	) -> None:

1	"""Suite-share endpoint tests against a real Postgres via TestClient.
2	
3	Access control needs *different* actors, so each request overrides
4	get_current_user to the acting user (the dev-bypass default is bypassed). The
5	owner is a real User; B/C/E are other users; a connection + suite are seeded
6	directly. Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
7	"""
8	
9	import uuid
10	from collections.abc import Iterator
11	from typing import Any
12	
13	import pytest
14	from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
15	
16	from backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user
17	from backend.app.db.models import Connection, Suite, User
18	from backend.app.db.session import get_db
19	from backend.app.main import app
20	
21	
22	@pytest.fixture
23	def client(db_session: Any) -> Iterator[TestClient]:
24	    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session
25	    try:
26	        yield TestClient(app)
27	    finally:
28	        app.dependency_overrides.clear()
29	
30	
31	def _user(db_session: Any, email: str) -> User:
32	    u = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=email)
33	    db_session.add(u)
34	    db_session.flush()
35	    return u
36	
37	
38	def _seed(db_session: Any) -> tuple[User, User, User, User, Suite]:
39	    owner = _user(db_session, "owner@ex")
40	    b = _user(db_session, "b@ex")
41	    c = _user(db_session, "c@ex")
42	    e = _user(db_session, "e@ex")  # no access
43	    conn = Connection(
44	        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
45	        type="snowflake",
46	        env="dev",
47	        config={"account": "x"},
48	        created_by=owner.id,
49	    )
50	    db_session.add(conn)
51	    db_session.flush()
52	    suite = Suite(name="finance", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
53	    db_session.add(suite)
54	    db_session.commit()
55	    return owner, b, c, e, suite
56	
57	
58	def _as(user: User) -> None:
59	    app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: user
60

68	    resp = client.post(

70	    )

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/user_service.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"User directory lookup — search the single-tenant user table.\n\nThe sharing UI grants access by `user_id`, but a human only knows an email or\nname; this is the search that turns one into the other. Single tenant, so any\nauthenticated user may search the whole directory — there is no per-tenant\nscoping to apply. FastAPI-free: takes a `Session` + query string.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom sqlalchemy import func, or_, select\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.db.models import User\n\n# A short query would match most of the directory; require enough to be a real\n# prefix/substring before we run the scan.\nMIN_QUERY_LEN = 2\n# Cap the result set so a broad term can't return the whole directory in one go.\nMAX_LIMIT = 50\nDEFAULT_LIMIT = 20\n\n\ndef _escape_like(term: str) -> str:\n    r\"\"\"Escape LIKE wildcards so a user's literal `%` / `_` / `\\` stays literal.\"\"\"\n    return term.replace(\"\\\\\", \"\\\\\\\\\").replace(\"%\", \"\\\\%\").replace(\"_\", \"\\\\_\")\n\n\ndef search_users(session: Session, query: str, *, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT) -> list[User]:\n    \"\"\"Find users whose email or display name contains `query` (case-insensitive).\n\n    Returns `[]` for a query shorter than `MIN_QUERY_LEN` (the caller's\n    type-ahead simply shows nothing until enough is typed). `limit` is clamped\n    to `[1, MAX_LIMIT]`. Results are ordered by email for a stable list.\n    \"\"\"\n    term = query.strip()\n    if len(term) < MIN_QUERY_LEN:\n        return []\n    capped = max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT))\n    pattern = f\"%{_escape_like(term)}%\"\n    stmt = (\n        select(User)\n        .where(\n            or_(\n                User.email.ilike(pattern, escape=\"\\\\\"),\n                func.coalesce(User.display_name, \"\").ilike(pattern, escape=\"\\\\\"),\n            )\n        )\n        .order_by(User.email)\n        .limit(capped)\n    )\n    return list(session.scalars(stmt))\n"
}
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/api/v1/users.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"User directory endpoints — search users to grant suite access to.\n\nThe sharing UI keys shares on a raw `user_id`, but a human picks a collaborator\nby email/name; this endpoint is the type-ahead behind that picker. Single\ntenant, so any authenticated user may search the directory. Only a minimal\npublic summary (id / email / display_name) is exposed — never AAD object ids or\ntimestamps.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Annotated\nfrom uuid import UUID\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Query\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user\nfrom backend.app.db.models import User\nfrom backend.app.db.session import get_db\nfrom backend.app.services import user_service as svc\n\nrouter = APIRouter(tags=[\"users\"])\n\n\nclass UserSummary(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"The public sliver of a user safe to expose in the directory picker.\"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)\n\n    id: UUID\n    email: str\n    display_name: str | None\n\n\n@router.get(\n    \"/users/search\",\n    response_model=list[UserSummary],\n    summary=\"Search the user directory by email or display name\",\n)\ndef search_users(\n    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],\n    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],\n    q: Annotated[str, Query(description=\"Email or name substring (min 2 chars).\")] = \"\",\n    limit: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=svc.MAX_LIMIT)] = svc.DEFAULT_LIMIT,\n) -> list[UserSummary]:\n    users = svc.search_users(db, q, limit=limit)\n    return [UserSummary.model_validate(u) for u in users]\n"
}

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: db_session\n    try:\n        yield TestClient(app)\n    finally:\n        app.dependency_overrides.clear()\n\n\ndef _user(db_session: Any, email: str, {
  "command": "cat > /tmp/pr_e2_body.md <<'EOF'\n## What & why\n\nUnblocks the **sharing/admin UI** (PR-E3) by filling the two backend gaps that made it impossible: shares keyed on a raw `user_id` UUID with no way to *find* a user, and a `ShareRead` that returned only that UUID so a collaborator list couldn't be named.\n\n### 1. `GET /api/v1/users/search` — directory type-ahead\n- Case-insensitive substring over `email` **and** `display_name`.\n- FastAPI-free `user_service.search_users` (mirrors the other service/router splits).\n- 2-char minimum (a shorter query returns `[]`), result limit clamped to `≤50`, query-param bound rejects over-cap `limit` with 422.\n- LIKE wildcards (`%` / `_` / `\\`) in the query are escaped — a literal `%` can't match the directory.\n- Returns a minimal `{id, email, display_name}` summary — never AAD object ids or timestamps.\n- Single-tenant: any authenticated user may search (no per-tenant scoping to apply).\n\n### 2. `ShareRead` enriched with grantee identity\n- Read-only joined `Share.user` relationship (ORM-only — **no migration / schema change**).\n- `ShareRead` gains `email` + `display_name`, built via an explicit `from_share` constructor (Pydantic `from_attributes` won't traverse `share.user.email`).\n- Grant / list / update all return the enriched shape, so the panel names each collaborator without a second lookup.\n\n## Tests\n- `tests/api/test_users.py` (8): email + display_name match, case-insensitivity, min-length floor, blank query, summary field allow-list, limit cap (422 + count), LIKE-escape.\n- `tests/api/test_shares.py`: existing 13 still green; grant test now asserts the enriched `email`/`display_name`.\n- Full `tests/api` suite: 160 passed.\n\n## Verification\nLocal: Black, Ruff, mypy, Bandit all clean on the changed files; API tests green against Postgres.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\nEOF\ngh pr create --base main --head feature/pr-e2-user-search-share-enrich \\\n  --title \"feat(backend): user-search endpoint + enriched ShareRead (PR-E2)\" \\\n  --body-file /tmp/pr_e2_body.md \\\n  --milestone \"Week 4 — Connection manager UI + check editor UI (frontend)\" 2>&1 | tail -4",

}

diff --git a/backend/app/api/v1/users.py b/backend/app/api/v1/users.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..884a09d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/backend/app/api/v1/users.py
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+"""User directory endpoints — search users to grant suite access to.
+
+The sharing UI keys shares on a raw `user_id`, but a human picks a collaborator
+by email/name; this endpoint is the type-ahead behind that picker. Single
+tenant, so any authenticated user may search the directory. Only a minimal
+public summary (id / email / display_name) is exposed — never AAD object ids or
+timestamps.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Annotated
+from uuid import UUID
+
+from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Query
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+
+from backend.app.core.auth import get_current_user
+from backend.app.db.models import User
+from backend.app.db.session import get_db
+from backend.app.services import user_service as svc
+
+router = APIRouter(tags=["users"])
+
+
+class UserSummary(BaseModel):
+    """The public sliver of a user safe to expose in the directory picker."""
+
+    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)
+
+    id: UUID
+    email: str
+    display_name: str | None
+
+
+@router.get(
+    "/users/search",
+    response_model=list[UserSummary],
+    summary="Search the user directory by email or display name",
+)
+def search_users(
+    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
+    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
+    q: Annotated[str, Query(description="Email or name substring (min 2 chars).")] = "",
+    limit: Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=svc.MAX_LIMIT)] = svc.DEFAULT_LIMIT,
+) -> list[UserSummary]:
+    users = svc.search_users(db, q, limit=limit)
+    return [UserSummary.model_validate(u) for u in users]

diff --git a/backend/app/services/user_service.py b/backend/app/services/user_service.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..49167ae
--- /dev/null
+++ b/backend/app/services/user_service.py
@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+"""User directory lookup — search the single-tenant user table.
+
+The sharing UI grants access by `user_id`, but a human only knows an email or
+name; this is the search that turns one into the other. Single tenant, so any
+authenticated user may search the whole directory — there is no per-tenant
+scoping to apply. FastAPI-free: takes a `Session` + query string.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from sqlalchemy import func, or_, select
+from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
+
+from backend.app.db.models import User
+
+# A short query would match most of the directory; require enough to be a real
+# prefix/substring before we run the scan.
+MIN_QUERY_LEN = 2
+# Cap the result set so a broad term can't return the whole directory in one go.
+MAX_LIMIT = 50
+DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20
+
+
+def _escape_like(term: str) -> str:
+    r"""Escape LIKE wildcards so a user's literal `%` / `_` / `\` stays literal."""
+    return term.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_")
+
+
+def search_users(session: Session, query: str, *, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT) -> list[User]:
+    """Find users whose email or display name contains `query` (case-insensitive).
+
+    Returns `[]` for a query shorter than `MIN_QUERY_LEN` (the caller's
+    type-ahead simply shows nothing until enough is typed). `limit` is clamped
+    to `[1, MAX_LIMIT]`. Results are ordered by email for a stable list.
+    """
+    term = query.strip()
+    if len(term) < MIN_QUERY_LEN:
+        return []
+    capped = max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT))
+    pattern = f"%{_escape_like(term)}%"
+    stmt = (
+        select(User)
+        .where(
+            or_(
+                User.email.ilike(pattern, escape="\\"),
+                func.coalesce(User.display_name, "").ilike(pattern, escape="\\"),
+            )
+        )
+        .order_by(User.email)
+        .limit(capped)
+    )
+    return list(session.scalars(stmt))
